He brings a consistent feel for developing routes and the length to disrupt the football at the catch point. His instincts have consistently improved since joining the Longhorns in 2023, which has become obvious this fall.

Prospects Considered : Edge Kenyatta Jackson, Ohio State; OL Anthonie Knapp, Notre Dame

23. Cincinnati Bengals: IOL Anthonie Knapp, Notre Dame

Team Fit : Cincinnati Bengals center Ted Karras and right guard Dalton Risner aren't signed beyond this season. Notre Dame's Anthonie Knapp can inject the team's offensive line with some youth and explosiveness off the snap. Knapp has flourished this fall after converting from left tackle to guard. He can immediately step in and give the Bengals an impressive trio alongside Amarius Mims and left guard Dylan Fairchild to provide a strong long-term foundation up front.

Scout's Take: Knapp is a sturdy, tone-setting presence at guard, with the play-strength and demeanor that fit the mold of a 'start and forget'-caliber prospect—which every team could use, especially one like Cincinnati with an offense centered around elite skill positions.

Prospects Considered : RB Jadan Baugh, Florida; S KJ Bolden, Georgia

24. Kansas City Chiefs: WR Cam Coleman, Texas

Team Fit : Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs can't threaten opponents vertically like the team's offense once did. Mahomes hasn't even tried to push the ball down the field in recent weeks . A legitimate presence on the outside with the capability of winning on deep routes is an absolute necessity going into next offseason. Enter Texas' Cam Coleman.

Scout's Take: Coleman is a height/weight/speed receiving prospect. The Texas target has outstanding ball skills to dominate at the catch point. The 6'3" receiver is a long-strider who will gallop past off-the-ball corners. Plus, he has the all-around traits to eventually develop into a true WR1 if he adds more tempo and nuance to his route-running.

Prospects Considered : OT Elijah Paige, USC; S Brauntae Johnson, Notre Dame

25. Philadelphia Eagles (via Jacksonville): QB LaNorris Sellers, South Carolina

Team Fit : Once upon a time, Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman drafted Jalen Hurts despite Carson Wentz already being on the team's roster and signed to a long-term contract. Less than a year later, Wentz was gone and Hurts became the team's starting quarterback. With the uncertainty surrounding Hurts' health and his inconsistent play over the last two seasons, Roseman should strongly consider a similar approach, particularly with an extra first-round pick now in the team's back pocket.

Scout's Take: LaNorris Sellers epitomizes a traits-based prospect. The South Carolina quarterback has elite arm strength to attack the entire field. His touch has improved this season as well. More importantly, the 21-year-old signal-caller has cleaned up his footwork and weight transfer when working from inside the pocket to create more consistency than previously seen. To top it all off, Sellers is a high-end athlete with the rushing/scrambling ability to take over games. As a result, he presents arguably the highest ceiling of any prospect in next year's class.

Prospects Considered : Edge Yhonzae Pierre, Alabama; CB Zabien Brown, Alabama

26. Pittsburgh Steelers: QB CJ Carr, Notre Dame

Team Fit : The Pittsburgh Steelers could realistically decide they prefer Drew Allar's development and allow the 2026 third-round draft pick to start next season. As of now, Aaron Rodgers' retirement is the only inevitability regarding the situation. So, the Steelers invest in the quarterback position again to ensure it's addressed long term. Allar can then compete with Notre Dame's CJ Carr if the organization likes both that much.

Scout's Take: Carr is an efficient pocket passer, who excels with timing and rhythm. Carr plays with sound mechanics and pocket navigation. He anticipates throwing lanes well and adjusts to post-snap coverages. His physical peak aligns with a more athletic Kirk Cousins. Essentially, Carr is a point guard-style passer, who can run the offense with clean, mistake-free play.

Prospects Considered : CB Jyaire Hill, Michigan; S Brauntae Johnson, Notre Dame

27. Detroit Lions: Edge Yhonzae Pierre, Alabama

Team Fit : As DJ Wonnum deals with an injury, second-round rookie Derrick Moore experienced a breakout game Sunday by providing a pair of sacks against the Miami Dolphins. Even so, the Detroit Lions have long attempted to address their pass rush beyond Aidan Hutchinson. Even if Moore continues to build on his latest performance, Wonnum is a pending free agent and the team could definitely use more depth to boost its pass rush.

Scout's Take: Yhonzae Pierre started the season hot but has cooled off over the last several weeks. Still, his athleticism and ability to convert speed to power are well worth a late first-round bet. The Alabama product is also comfortable dropping into coverage, with a pick-six and four passes defended this season. That versatility gives him the potential to become a multifaceted impact defender at the next level.

Prospects Considered : TE Trey'Dez Green, LSU; CB Jyaire Hill, Michigan

28. Minnesota Vikings: RB Jadan Baugh, Florida

Team Fit : With a half-dozen quarterbacks already off the board, the Minnesota Vikings must go in another direction. The organization can eventually pursue veteran options, like Mac Jones or Davis Mills, or bring back Kirk Cousins for another year. Then, the draft can supply a different offensive focal point by adding the class' RB1. Florida's Jadan Baugh can serve as an every-down workhorse to offset any lingering issues at the game's most important position.

Scout's Take: Baugh is a physical running back with light, quick footwork. He has the lateral agility to make defenders miss and force missed tackles at all three levels. While the Florida back hasn't seen much passing-game usage this season, he showed his value out of the backfield in 2025 with 33 receptions. Once Baugh develops as a pass protector, he will be viewed as a complete back.

Prospects Considered : TE Trey'Dez Green, LSU; OL Trevor Lauck, Iowa

29. Denver Broncos: TE Trey'Dez Green, LSU

Team Fit : The Denver Broncos' Sean Payton should be all aflutter thinking of using LSU's Trey'Dez Green in a similar fashion to when the head coach had Jimmy Graham in the New Orleans Saints' offense. The Broncos haven't gotten much from the tight end position this season. Plus, veteran Evan Engram isn't signed beyond the 2026 campaign. Green can provide a massive target to also offset the decline of wide receiver Courtland Sutton.

Scout's Take: There's some real size at the tight end position in next year's class. The 6'7", 240-pound Green serves as the prime example. He's an instant mismatch even if he's still learning the nuances of the position. To Green's credit, he has a natural feel for manipulation tactics at the top of his routes. Thus, he becomes a problem when working downfield and after the catch.

Prospects Considered : WR Nick Marsh, Indiana; OT Elijah Paige, USC

30. Tennessee Titans (via Chicago): OT Elijah Paige, USC

Team Fit : In order for Cam Ward to develop, the Tennessee Titans must properly protect the 2025 No. 1 overall pick. Left tackle Dan Moore Jr. is a replacement-level performer at best. The Titans can solidify the left side of their offensive line by placing USC's Elijah Paige next to standout left guard Peter Skoronski and make life a little easier for Ward.

Scout's Take: Paige is a thick, wide-bodied tackle with an easy anchor and enough movement skills to cut off and absorb defenders at a high level. Unrefined aspects of his game often seen in his footwork and aiming points can sap his raw talent. However, with ideal size and the ability to root his feet and take ground when needed, a recipe exists for the 21-year-old to start right away thanks to a considerably higher ceiling than most late first-round tackles possess.

Prospects Considered : RB Dylan Riley, Boise State; WR KJ Duff, Rutgers

31. San Francisco 49ers: IOL Kade Pieper, Iowa

Team Fit : The San Francisco 49ers don't require premium talent along their offensive line for Kyle Shanahan's offense to excel. It can help and expand the scheme, though. Veteran center Jake Brendel is a free agent after this season. Left guard can also be upgraded. Iowa's Kade Pieper could take over either spot. He could be particularly effective if asked to transition over the ball.

Scout's Take: Pieper is a tailor-made fit for the traditional Shanahan-style offense predicated on schematic guardrails in pass protection with a diverse, zone-oriented run game. Thanks to elite-level burst, quickness and a red-hot motor as a finisher, Pieper's lack of sand and bulk is often hidden enough to allow his strengths to shine inside Iowa's zone-heavy, run-first scheme. His fit in San Francisco, while moving him to center, should maximize Pieper's NFL potential.

Prospects Considered : DL Jayden Jackson, Oklahoma; S KJ Bolden, Georgia

32. Buffalo Bills: S Brauntae Johnson, Notre Dame

Team Fit : The Buffalo Bills' safeties continue to play poorly. The team hasn't been quite right along its back line since the tandem of Micah Hyde and Jordan Poyer patrolled the space. Notre Dame's Brauntae Johnson continues to recover from an early-season foot injury and has barely played. However, he entered the campaign as the class' top safety prospect. Plus, a return is expected, particularly with the Fighting Irish in the mix for a national championship.

Scout's Take: Physicality and size in the run game, paired with instinctual play on the back end, make a healthy Johnson a true impact playmaker. His unique blend of movement skills, raw talent and leadership is still needed in the Notre Dame secondary this season. Then, those same traits will help any NFL defensive backfield.

Prospects Considered : WR KJ Duff, Rutgers; OL Trevor Lauck, Iowa

articles.title: 2027 NFL Free Agency Big Board After Trade Deadline Passes
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline was a wild affair, with several big-name players being moved in blockbuster fashion. Now that the trade window has closed, so too has the opportunity to add premium veteran talent for the remainder of 2026.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline was a wild affair, with several big-name players being moved in blockbuster fashion. Now that the trade window has closed, so too has the opportunity to add premium veteran talent for the remainder of 2026.

However, teams looking to improve for the 2027 season won't have to wait long for their chance. The new league year and free agency will officially open at 4 p.m. ET on March 11. The legal-contact window will open two days prior.

That's only four months from now, for those keeping track.

The good news for teams hoping to stock up for a 2027 run is that next year's free-agent class is loaded with high-level starters and quality role players.

Here, we'll take an early look at the 2027 free-agent class and rank the top 50 players based on factors such as past production, player upside, age, positional value, positional market depth, and player health. You'll also find contract projections and potential suitors for the top 10 headliners.

Quarterback Kyler Murray hasn't exactly reestablished himself as a premier starter with the Minnesota Vikings this season. However, he's still a former Pro Bowler and a viable dual-threat signal-caller who won't turn 30 until August. He should draw interest as a bridge option from quarterback-needy teams.

49. Daron Payne, DT, Washington Commanders

Daron Payne is currently on injured reserve with a fracture in his left foot. However, the 29-year-old has regularly been among the league's most disruptive interior defenders when healthy. In six games before the injury, he recorded 14 tackles, a sack, and nine quarterback pressures.

48. Chase McLaughlin, K, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Kickers aren't typically viewed as premier free-agent targets. However, any team that has experienced kicking woes in 2026 will tell you that good kickers are a valuable commodity. Chase McLaughlin has been one of the league's best this season. At age 30, he should have several more strong seasons ahead of him.

47. Arik Armstead, DL, Jacksonville Jaguars

Defensive lineman Arik Armstead will turn 33 this month and may not excel in any one area. However, he remains a full-time starter for the Jacksonville Jaguars, who can do a little bit of everything and do it well.

Ikem Ekwonu is a bit of a wild card, as he remains sidelined with a torn patellar tendon in his right knee from last season's playoffs. However, starting-caliber left tackles aren't easy to find. Ekwonu has started all 65 games he's appeared in (including playoffs).

Having turned only 26 in October, Ekwonu will interest a lot of teams as long as he's healthy at the start of the offseason.

The running back position has seen a bit of a value bump over the last couple of years, as Tony Pollard remains a quality starter. He can get tough yards, break long runs, and catch passes out of the backfield. While he'll turn 30 in April, he has remained a high-volume back for the Tennessee Titans in 2026.

44. Patrick Queen, LB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Patrick Queen entered the NFL as a first-round pick out of LSU in 2020. While he has never quite played up to his draft status, he has established himself as a quality starter with a pair of Pro Bowls on his resume. So far this season, he has recorded 60 tackles and 2.5 sacks while allowing an opposing passer rating of just 51.4 in coverage.

43. Kevin Byard, S, New England Patriots

Safety Kevin Byard may be 33 years old, but he remains a starting-caliber safety and has fared very well in his first season with the New England Patriots. The three-time first-team All-Pro brings both production and versatility to the position and should interest several teams on a one- or two-year deal.

42. Kayvon Thibodeaux, Edge, New York Giants

The New York Giants drafted Kayvon Thibodeaux fifth overall in 2022. Their investment hasn't quite paid off, as the Oregon product has reached double-digit sacks only once in his career. Still, he possesses plenty of physical upside and will only turn 26 in December.

41. Frankie Luvu, LB, Washington Commanders

Frankie Luvu brings a ton of versatility to his position. He has played both inside and outside as an off-ball linebacker and served as an edge defender—one who logged eight sacks and 18 QB pressures in 2024. He was limited by a groin injury early in the season, but he is healthy now and is still only 30 years old.

40. K'Lavon Chaisson, Edge, Washington Commanders

K'Lavon Chaisson was a first-round pick in 2020 but has really come into his own as a pass-rusher over the past few seasons. After recording just five sacks in his first four seasons, he logged 5.5 with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2023 and 7.5 with the Patriots last year. The 27-year-old is on pace for another seven-sack season with Washington this year.

39. DaVon Hamilton, DL, Jacksonville Jaguars

DaVon Hamilton recently landed on injured reserve with a torn quad. However, the longtime Jaguars starter was in the midst of another strong campaign when he got injured. The 29-year-old started all seven games in which he appeared and was graded 18th overall among interior defenders by Pro Football Focus after Week 8.

A massive (6'4", 335 lbs) run stopper on the interior, Hamilton should draw significant interest as long as his recovery goes smoothly.

38. Malcolm Koonce, Edge, Las Vegas Raiders

Maxx Crosby rightfully gets all of the attention whenever the Las Vegas Raiders' pass rush is discussed. However, Malcolm Koonce has been a vastly underrated complement when healthy over the past few seasons. He's still only 28 years old.

Safety Jeremy Chinn is another underrated member of the Raiders' defense who may garner more interest than many might expect on the open market. He can fill a variety of roles on the back end of a defense and won't turn 29 until February.

Los Angeles Rams receiver Davante Adams will turn 34 in December and is currently sidelined with a significant hamstring injury. His allure in free agency will largely hinge on how he performs after his expected return later in the season.

Before the injury, though, Adams was fantastic, catching 30 balls for 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games.

35. T.J. Hockenson, TE, Minnesota Vikings

Over the past few seasons, T.J. Hockenson has largely been overshadowed by Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison in Minnesota's offense. However, he's an above-average starting tight end who can block with the best of them and create legitimate mismatches in the passing game.

34. Dre Greenlaw, LB, San Francisco 49ers

Linebacker Dre Greenlaw landed back with the San Francisco 49ers in the offseason. He's been spectacular when healthy. In seven starts, the 29-year-old has recorded 57 tackles, three tackles for loss, 27 solo stops, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery. He has allowed an opposing passer rating of 89.4 in coverage.

Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown has seemingly regressed in the first half of 2026. However, he's still a capable dual-threat back who topped 1,300 scrimmage yards in both 2024 and 2025. He'll only turn 27 in March.

Ben Powers has been a decidedly average starter this season for the Denver Broncos. However, the market will be thin with starting-caliber offensive linemen. The 30-year-old has started all nine games in 2026 and has 91 career starts (including playoffs) on his resume.

31. Keisean Nixon, CB, Green Bay Packers

Keisean Nixon is a bit on the smaller side at 5'10" and 200 pounds. He won't be a fit for teams that prefer longer cornerbacks. However, the Green Bay Packers special-teams-ace-turned-starter can provide a lot of roster versatility.

A two-time first-team All-Pro as a return specialist, the 29-year-old can play inside and outside in a defense. He has allowed an opposing passer rating of just 73.6 this season.

30. Grover Stewart, DT, Indianapolis Colts

Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle Grover Stewart hasn't garnered as much attention as former teammate DeForest Buckner, who was just traded. However, the 3-year-old is a quality run-stuffer who has logged 28 tackles, a half-sack, and two tackles for loss this season.

29. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Khalil Mack is a future Hall of Famer. He also happens to be 35 years old and probably won't be a top target for teams seeking long-term options.

That said, Mack is still a very productive defender who will appeal to contenders. He's played on a winless defense in 2026 and has still notched 22 tackles, three sacks, five tackles for loss, and 11 quarterback pressures.

Riq Woolen has merely been a serviceable starter for the Philadelphia Eagles this season, though Philly's defense has been an overall disappointment. The 27-year-old notched 12 interceptions and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 70.6 in four seasons with the Seattle Seahawks. At 6'4" and 210 pounds, he'll interest teams that prefer bigger corners with ball skills.

27. Marlon Humphrey, CB, Baltimore Ravens

Marlon Humphrey will turn 31 next summer, but he remains an above-average starter. The four-time Pro Bowler has played 79 percent of the defensive snaps this season and has allowed an opposing passer rating of just 80.6 in coverage.

Josh Downs has been a fine complementary receiver in his four seasons with the Colts, though both he and Indy's offense have been in a bit of a slump this season. Despite being just 5'9" and 171 pounds, the 25-year-old has been a steady producer who has 2,494 receiving yards in 56 career games.

Downs was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs on Tuesday and could significantly boost his stock by playing with Patrick Mahomes over the second half of the season.

25. Uchenna Nwosu, Edge, Seattle Seahawks

Uchenna Nwosu is currently dealing with an ankle injury. Seattle will be happy to get him back in the pass-rushing rotation. He recorded seven sacks, seven tackles for loss, and 23 quarterback pressures last season.

Nwosu will turn 30 in December and should interest multiple teams seeking rotational edge help in the spring.

24. Jaylon Moore, OT, Kansas City Chiefs

Jaylon Moore is not an elite offensive tackle. However, he's a good starter who will likely cash in during an offseason with few free-agent options at the position. The former San Francisco 49ers backup has found a larger role with the Chiefs and is still only 28 years old.

23. DJ Turner II, CB, Cincinnati Bengals

D.J. Turner II entered the NFL as a second-round pick in 2023 out of Michigan. Since then, the 26-year-old has developed into a quality starter for the Bengals. He has started all eight games this season and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 81.6 in coverage.

Did Aaron Donald only return to the Rams for a one-year run? That question won't be answered until the offseason. If the 35-year-old is open to playing again next season, he'll be one of the top defenders available.

While the 10-time Pro Bowler hasn't been racking up stats the way he did early in his career, he's still more impactful than most interior defenders playing right now.

The 2027 free-agent class won't be loaded with top-tier offensive linemen, which will benefit players like Kevin Dotson. A full-time starter in L.A. since he arrived in 2023, Dotson has made 84 starts with the Rams and Steelers and only turned 30 in September.

20. YaYa Diaby, Edge, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

YaYa Diaby is currently out with an MCL sprain. However, he's been one of the league's most underrated edge defenders when healthy, pretty much since entering the league. He recorded 32 quarterback pressures in each of the past two seasons and has 22 sacks and 44 tackles for loss in 59 career regular-season games.

19. Blake Cashman, LB, Minnesota Vikings

Minnesota Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman is a do-it-all playmaker in the middle of the defense. The 30-year-old is on pace for his fourth straight campaign with at least 100 tackles. He's also been an effective situational pass-rusher in Brian Flores' defense.

18. Andrew Van Ginkel, Edge, Minnesota Vikings

Andrew Van Ginkel has been one of the league's better part-time pass-rushers for some time. He should be a coveted player despite the fact that he'll turn 32 in July. He recorded 18.5 sacks, 29 tackles for loss, and 42 quarterback pressures over the past two seasons, as he's on pace for another double-digit sack campaign.

Expect Kirk Cousins to interest most teams that plan to draft a quarterback highly in April. The 38-year-old has been an exemplary bridge quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders this season, playing at an above-average level while helping mentor first overall pick Fernando Mendoza .

Cousins was traded to the Vikings on Tuesday, and Minnesota will have a club option in 2027.

Mac Jones should be one of the top quarterbacks on the 2027 market. Depending on how next year's draft class shapes up, he could get multiple starting offers.

Jones was a rookie Pro Bowler with the New England Patriots in 2021 and struggled for several seasons before reemerging as San Francisco's spot starter last season. The 28-year-old went 5-3 with a 97.4 QB rating in 2026 and is due another opportunity to lead a franchise.

15. Jessie Bates III, S, Jacksonville Jaguars

Safety Jessie Bates III was traded from the Atlanta Falcons to Jacksonville on Monday. There's a reason why the Jaguars wanted the standout defender. Bates is a legitimate difference-maker at safety. The 29-year-old has 28 career interceptions and has a pick and three forced fumbles this season.

The Rams could potentially lose both of their starting guards in free agency. Teams will covet Steve Avila most. He's been a well-above-average starter for most of his four-year career. He only turned 27 in late October.

13. DeForest Buckner, DT, San Francisco 49ers

DeForest Buckner began his career with the 49ers as the seventh overall pick in the 2016 draft. He was dealt in 2020 but returned to San Francisco this season in another trade. The 32-year-old has been a disruptive front-line defender throughout his career and is already up to 32 tackles and four sacks in 2026.

Brian Branch would probably already have a second contract if he hadn't suffered a torn Achilles last season. He was a Defensive Rookie of the Year finalist in 2023 and a Pro Bowler in 2024, but last year's injury left some uncertainty as the Alabama product became extension-eligible in the offseason.

Branch is healthy now, though, and has recorded 14 tackles and an interception while allowing an opposing passer rating of only 20.8 in three games since his return. He only turned 25 in October.

A 2023 third-round pick out of Iowa, Riley Moss has established himself as a quality perimeter starter in Denver's defense. The 26-year-old has been heavily tested while playing opposite Patrick Surtain II and has rarely flinched. He's a rangy corner at 6'0", 193 pounds, who will only turn 27 in March.

Contract Projection: Three Years, $78 Million

We haven't seen much of guard Quenton Nelson since the Colts traded him to the Seahawks. He started for Seattle in Week 8 and then underwent a " minor procedure " on his knee.

The good news is that Nelson isn't expected to land on injured reserve. The knee shouldn't be a significant concern in the spring. If healthy, the eight-time Pro Bowler could be the top offensive lineman on the 2027 market.

Sunday's game was the first that Nelson has missed due to injury since 2023. He's made the Pro Bowl every year of his career and is a three-time first-team All-Pro. Pro Football Focus graded him third overall among all qualifying guards entering Week 9.

At 30, Nelson may not command a lengthy contract. However, he should earn a top-tier deal and garner attention from almost every team in need of a starting guard.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers

Contract Projection: Four Years, $110 Million

Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. could have earned a new contract with the Steelers this past offseason, but he never seemed happy with Pittsburgh's offer. He missed the beginning of the season while dealing with a back injury and was eventually traded to the Dallas Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.

According to Chris Mack of Kaboly and Mack , there was a "belief" that Porter was holding out for a $30 million-per-year offer.

Porter may fall a bit short of that mark on the open market. He's shown flashes in Dallas, but he hasn't turned the Cowboys' defense into a playoff-caliber unit. He's also currently battling an ankle injury.

That said, Porter should still be the top cornerback on the market if Dallas doesn't lock him up first. He's a terrific cover corner who is just a notch below the elite tier—he allowed an opposing passer rating of only 57.1 last season—and he'll only turn 27 in July.

Potential Suitors: Detroit Lions, Washington Commanders

Contract Projection: Four Years, $112 Million

Moro Ojomo hasn't gotten as much attention as fellow Eagles defensive linemen Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis—and the Eagles haven't given him a hefty second contract yet, either. However, he should be in the spotlight more following Monday's trade of Davis to Jacksonville.

Ojomo is definitely going to get a ton of attention from teams in need of interior defensive help in the spring.

The 2023 seventh-round pick should be highly coveted, as Milton Williams was a couple of offseasons ago. Contract offers will reflect that.

Ojomo's numbers are down a bit this season, as is Philadelphia's overall defensive performance. However, he continues to be a disruptive and multifaceted interior defender who can eat blocks, clog lanes, collapse the pocket, pressure quarterbacks, and end plays in the backfield.

Ojomo finished last season with 38 tackles, six sacks, six tackles for loss, and 21 quarterback pressures. He won't turn 26 until August.

Potential Suitors: Green Bay Packers, Miami Dolphins

7. Parker Washington, WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Contract Projection: Four Years, $108 Million

Parker Washington's ascent to stardom has been both unexpected and thrilling to watch. The 2023 sixth-round pick out of Penn State has gone from an overlooked addition to the Jaguars' biggest offensive threat in no time.

Despite having a running-back build (5'10", 204 lbs) and a lack of elite athletic traits, Washington has developed into one of the most difficult pass-catchers to defend in the league. Savvy route-running and a knack for finding space in the secondary allow him to operate as a high-volume inside-outside receiver.

When Washington gets the ball in stride, he has the play speed needed to make defenses pay.

After catching 58 passes for 847 yards and five touchdowns in 2025, Washington is on pace to eclipse those numbers in 2026. He has 29 catches for 493 yards and five touchdowns through eight games, cementing himself as Jacksonville's No. 1 target.

While a lack of elite size may keep Washington out of the upper tier of receiver contracts, the 24-year-old should command a deal that falls somewhere between those signed by Wan'Dale Robinson and Alec Pierce this past offseason.

Potential Suitors: Los Angeles Chargers, Los Angeles Rams

6. Tuli Tuipulotu, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Contract Projection: Four Years, $92 Million

Chargers edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu might not be a household name, but you can bet that teams are well aware of the 24-year-old. A 2023 second-round pick out of USC, Tuipulotu has emerged as one of Los Angeles' most impactful defenders over the past four years.

Tuipulotu is a big (6'3", 266 lbs) and physical edge defender who possesses the athleticism to serve as a rush linebacker and the strength to play along the defensive line. He can disengage blockers with good use of his hands, beat blockers with counter moves, and collapse the pocket with very good play strength.

The Chargers' defense has disappointed in 2026, but Tuipulotu racked up 49 tackles, 13 sacks, 20 tackles for loss, and 32 quarterback pressures last season. His sack numbers are down a bit this year, but he's still playing at a Pro Bowl level.

Tuipulotu can fit a variety of defensive schemes. He possesses a very attractive combination of ability and youth. He's likely to be one of the first defenders signed in free agency if L.A. doesn't lock him up before the contract window.

Potential Suitors: Cincinnati Bengals, Las Vegas Raiders

Contract Projection: Four Years, $76 Million

There was some uncertainty about Sam LaPorta's future last season, as he dealt with a herniated spinal disc that ended his campaign prematurely. However, the 25-year-old has been back and as good as ever through the first half of 2026.

While the Lions have made a habit of extending key players early, they have yet to lock up their star tight end—possibly because of the cloud of last year's injury. LaPorta, though, has said his lack of a new deal isn't a distraction.

"If I don't get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else," LaPorta said on Pardon My Take (h/t ProFootballTalk's Michael David Smith ).

While the 6'3", 245-pound LaPorta may not be an elite run blocker, he's a true mismatch as a receiver. The Iowa product has been a huge part of what Detroit likes to do offensively, but he's correct in his belief that he can get a payday elsewhere.

Expect cap-rich teams in need of offensive playmakers to line up with offers for LaPorta.

Potential Suitors: Cincinnati Bengals, Miami Dolphins

Contract Projection: Four Years, $120 Million

Jared Verse was the star of the Rams' pass-rushing rotation before he was dealt to the Cleveland Browns as part of the Myles Garrett trade. However, it was teammate Byron Young who led the team in sacks last season with 12.

Young, a 2023 third-round pick out of Tennessee, has been a defensive force since joining L.A. Over his first three years, he compiled an impressive 27.5 sacks, 32 tackles for loss, four forced fumbles, and 93 quarterback pressures. He's having another strong season despite playing most of the season without a top-tier bookend like Verse or Garrett opposite him.

If there's a knock on Young, it's that he entered the league as an older prospect and will turn 29 in March. However, it doesn't change the fact that he's an athletic and powerful 6'2", 260-pound defender with a high motor who can consistently disrupt opposing game plans.

Young will be the top edge defender on a lot of boards in the spring. He should command a contract similar to the one that Jaelan Phillips received this past offseason.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Washington Commanders

Contract Projection: Four Years, $128 Million

Kobie Turner has spent a little less time in the spotlight this season due to the return of Aaron Donald. He's also currently on injured reserve with a groin strain.

However, this shouldn't significantly dampen his value on the open market.

Turner has yet to earn a Pro Bowl nod, but the 2023 third-round pick has consistently played at a Pro Bowl level since entering the league. In each of his first three seasons, Turner recorded at least 48 tackles, seven sacks, eight tackles for loss, and 20 quarterback pressures.

At 6'2" and 294 pounds, Turner is rarely the biggest player on the field, but he consistently wins with good athleticism, a solid base, great play strength and hand usage, and a high motor.

Set to turn 28 in April, Turner could be the most coveted defender on the market.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Las Vegas Raiders

Contract Projection: Four Years, $140 Million

George Pickens might not be the top wide receiver available on the 2027 market, but that won't prevent him from being the top target for a lot of teams. He's been an elite No. 2 receiver for the Dallas Cowboys. He will only turn 26 in March.

Pickens showed last season that he's even capable of putting up No. 1 receiver numbers. He filled the role for a few games when CeeDee Lamb was sidelined and finished with 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. It was the second campaign in four seasons with at least 1,100 yards for the Georgia product.

While Pickens hasn't been quite as prolific this year, he's on pace for another 1,000-yard season.

With a great blend of speed, size (6'3", 200 lbs), and contested-catch ability, Pickens should heavily interest teams that need a go-to target and don't want to dish out a market-topping contract. On the open market, he should fall somewhere in the range of Lamb, Garrett Wilson, and Zay Flowers.

That is, if the Cowboys don't give him the franchise tag for the second straight offseason.

Potential Suitors: Los Angeles Chargers, Las Vegas Raiders

Contract Projection: Four Years, $165 Million

Puka Nacua might be just a bit behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the NFL's wide receiver hierarchy, but he isn't a distant second. The 25-year-old would probably already rival Smith-Njigba in terms of salary, if not for a few specific factors.

For one, Nacua does have a fairly extensive injury history and has missed time every year except his 2023 rookie campaign. He's currently sidelined with MCL and PCL sprains that he suffered on Sunday.

Nacua is also on a team that shelled out for several big-name players in order to chase a Super Bowl in 2026.

Given Los Angeles' investments and lengthy list of standout 2027 free agents, Nacua will be a prime candidate for the franchise tag this offseason. If he hits the market, though, he should be the top target for receiver-needy teams.

Nacua is a master of route-running, spatial awareness, and body control. Combined with a 6'2" frame and excellent play speed, these skills make Nacua one of the biggest mismatches in the league.

Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches and 107.2 receiving yards per game last season. He's off to another strong start in 2026. He's less than 100 yards away from eclipsing 5,000 career receiving yards—which he should do before the end of his fourth season—and he won't turn 26 until next May.

Expect most cap-rich teams with a need for receiver depth to have Nacua at the top of their boards.

Potential Suitors: Miami Dolphins, Washington Commanders

*Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference unless otherwise noted.

articles.title: B/R's Week 10 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: It seems like the 2026 season just started, but we're already at Week 10. The fantasy playoffs are closer than the season opener, and the final month of the fantasy regular season is nearly here.
articles.body:
It seems like the 2026 season just started, but we're already at Week 10. The fantasy playoffs are closer than the season opener, and the final month of the fantasy regular season is nearly here.

The stretch run has arrived—and it means different things for different managers.

Managers at 6-3 or better aren't just looking toward the playoffs. They are looking toward a first-round bye. Toward a championship.

Managers at 5-4 or 4-5 aren't thinking about championships right now. They are just looking to get a ticket to the dance. To earn a postseason berth, no matter the seed.

Those at 3-6 or worse? The playoffs likely aren't happening. Not this year. But there are games to be played. Dreams to ruin. Pride to be reclaimed.

Whatever the motivation, everyone's goal is the same in Week 10: victory.

Bleacher Report is here to help them get it with position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get to this week's sortable player rankings for PPR leagues in Week 10, a few quick notes.

The first never changes—the overall player rankings can aid with "flex" lineup decisions, but they do not include quarterbacks. If you play in a league with a "superflex" spot and have a viable QB2, he gets that flex spot over most players.

The second is that Week 10 is another four-team bye week—the Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers are all off. No Caleb Williams, Jonah Coleman, Saquon Barkley or Bucky Irving this week.

One final reminder: Even if you're sitting at 3-6 or worse and out of playoff contention, keep setting a competitive lineup. Staying active helps maintain a fair competition for your leaguemates and gives you a chance to play spoiler down the stretch.

There were some gaudy numbers posted by fantasy quarterbacks last week, but no signal-caller did more to help fantasy managers in Week 9 than Jordan Love of the Green Bay Packers.

Love carved up the New England Patriots with surgical precision at Gillette Stadium, hitting on multiple long throws to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden on the way to 372 passing yards and three scores. Love also added a rushing touchdown.

At the halfway point of the NFL season, Love is leading the NFL with 2,618 passing yards. The seventh-year veteran is on pace to shatter Aaron Rodgers' team record for passing yards in a season, and no quarterback in the NFC has more fantasy points this year.

The NFL trade deadline brought some movement at the quarterback position.

The Baltimore Ravens acquired Jacoby Brissett as a veteran stopgap while Lamar Jackson is out, and a Minnesota Vikings team seeking improved quarterback production sent a third-rounder to the Las Vegas Raiders for Kirk Cousins.

That wasn't the only change at quarterback. With Brissett in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew sidelined by a torn UCL, rookie Carson Beck is in line to make his first career start in Week 10. No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is also set for his first start following Cousins' trade.

The Giants, meanwhile, hope J.J. McCarthy will be available Thursday night after he suffered a hip injury against the Philadelphia Eagles. Miami's Malik Willis is headed to injured reserve with a core muscle injury.

Jordan Love may be rolling, but after a hot start to the season Patrick Mahomes is not. The Chiefs star sits dead-last among all qualifying quarterbacks in intended air yards per attempt, and he has failed to hit 16.5 fantasy points in three of four games since the bye.

That 16.5-point mark ranks outside the top 15 at the position in points per game.

Drake Maye, New England Patriots (at Detroit Lions)

Maye had a game to forget last week against the Packers, throwing three interceptions in the first half of a lopsided loss. But he also threw three touchdown passes in the game, and Sunday he faces a Detroit Lions team that leads the league in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.

Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

Love's recent production makes him difficult to bench, but this matchup warrants caution. Minnesota has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks and just held Buffalo's Josh Allen to his lowest fantasy total of the season. Green Bay's struggles running the ball could also leave Love with limited offensive support.

Drew Lock, Seattle Seahawks (at Las Vegas Raiders)

Lock's numbers have been modest in two of his three games so far this season. But in a plus matchup with the Arizona Cardinals in September, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns. Similar success is entirely possible Sunday against a Raiders team surrendering the third-most fantasy points per game to QBs.

The top of the running back rankings after nine weeks is mostly the usual suspects—Kenneth Walker III of the Kansas City Chiefs has exceeded expectations in 2026, but those expectations were still pretty high.

The expectations for Jaylen Warren of the Pittsburgh Steelers were more muted. The fifth-year veteran was the 27th player at his position taken on average over the summer.

Warren has soared past that ADP. He's the RB13 in PPR points, the RB10 in PPR points per game and since Week 3 he's one of four backs who is averaging 20-plus PPR points per game.

That's the kind of value that wins fantasy leagues.

There were rumors galore that fantasy-relevant running backs could be dealt at the deadline, with Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts, Derrick Henry of the Baltimore Ravens and Tony Pollard of the Tennessee Titans all mentioned as trade targets. In the end, it was much ado about nothing—none of those ball-carriers switched teams.

Several backfields suffered significant injuries in Week 9. Josh Jacobs of the Green Bay Packers suffered a fractured finger that required surgery, while Rhamondre Stevenson of the New England Patriots hurt his knee. Both are expected to miss multiple weeks.

A couple of struggling ground games got contributions from unlikely sources in Week 9. With Jacobs hurt, Kaleb Johnson assumed lead back duties for the Packers, rushing for 68 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries against the Patriots. Audric Estime led the New Orleans Saints in backfield touches against the Cleveland Browns, turning 16 into 77 yards and a score.

Zach Charbonnet, Seattle Seahawks (at Las Vegas Raiders)

Charbonnet has yet to find the end zone since returning to action, but he recorded 17 touches for 86 yards last week against the Arizona Cardinals. The fourth-year pro has a favorable opportunity to score this week against a Raiders defense allowing a league-high 151.2 rushing yards per game.

Chase Brown, Cincinnati Bengals (vs. Pittsburgh Steelers)

It has been a rough season for Brown, who is averaging a career-low 3.9 yards per carry and less than 50 yards on the ground per game. Things aren't going to get any easier in this week's big AFC North matchup with the rival Steelers—Pittsburgh is allowing fewer rushing yards per game than any team in the AFC.

Audric Estime, New Orleans Saints (vs. Carolina Panthers)

Estime came from nowhere to finish Week 9 as a top-10 running back in PPR points, and he should serve as at least a solid second starter for fantasy managers in Week 10 as well. The Carolina Panthers have given up the fifth-most rushing yards per game in 2026, and only one team has surrendered more PPR points per game to running backs.

Last week in Madrid, Ja'Marr Chase had eight catches for 142 yards—in the first half. That was the most receiving yards by a Bengals player in a half in almost four decades.

He finished the win over the Atlanta Falcons with 10 grabs for 155 yards and a touchdown. Those numbers ranked him fourth among wide receivers in PPR points for the week.

It marked the second consecutive week that Chase has topped 30 PPR points—a feat duplicated by only one other wideout this season: Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks.

In terms of PPR points per game, only Smith-Njigba has been more productive this year for fantasy managers than Puka Nacua of the Los Angeles Rams. But Nacua has a history of getting nicked up, and it happened again—fresh off the best score by a wide receiver in Week 9, Nacua is headed to injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.

Nacua was the biggest name at wide receiver that got hurt in Week 9, but he wasn't the only one. Luther Burden III of the Chicago Bears and Jaylen Waddle of the Denver Broncos are both on bye this week, which is good—because both receivers are in the concussion protocol. Xavier Worthy of the Kansas City Chiefs (hamstring) and Ladd McConkey of the Los Angeles Chargers (back) also went down with injuries a week ago.

The Chiefs made a deal to address the Worthy injury at the trade deadline, acquiring Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts.

The Colts also traded veteran Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers.

Denzel Boston, Cleveland Browns (vs. Houston Texans)

After catching six passes for 98 yards last week against the Saints, Boston now sits just outside the top-20 receivers in PPR points for the season. The second-round rookie should have another good game this week against a Texans team giving up the second-most PPR points per game to wideouts this season.

Drake London, Atlanta Falcons (vs. Kansas City Chiefs)

Most fantasy managers don't have the luxury of even thinking about sitting a receiver like London—especially in a four-team bye week. But London is barely averaging 6.5 PPR points over the past couple of games, and this week he draws the worst fantasy matchup in the AFC for his position.

Jakobi Meyers, Jacksonville Jaguars (at Tennessee Titans)

Parker Washington is Jacksonville's No. 1 wide receiver, but Meyers has also been productive, scoring double-digit PPR points in half his games this season. He has a favorable opportunity to reach that mark again in Week 10 against the Titans, the only team allowing more than 40 PPR points per game to wide receivers.

Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers leads his position in PPR points per game and is the only tight end averaging more than 20 this season.

However, a change at quarterback introduces some uncertainty. Rookie Fernando Mendoza will start when the Raiders host the Seattle Seahawks this week.

Bowers should remain a primary target, but his fantasy production will depend in part on how effectively Mendoza runs the passing game.

If the rookie struggles early, Bowers' fantasy value is going to take a hit.

Injuries spare no position, including tight ends. A down season for Jake Ferguson of the Dallas Cowboys got worse when Ferguson suffered a knee injury against the Indianapolis Colts that will sideline him indefinitely.

Terrance Ferguson of the Los Angeles Rams returned to practice just in time to strain his hamstring, and if he isn't activated soon his season will be over.

In Weeks 6-8 combined, Darren Waller of the Carolina Panthers had just two catches, although one was a long touchdown. But last week against the Denver Broncos, Waller blew up—10 targets, eight catches, 90 yards and a score on the way to the best fantasy line from a tight end.

After a slow start to the season, Kyle Pitts put together a productive stretch. However, his three catches for 23 yards last week marked his second consecutive game—and fifth this season—with fewer than six PPR points.

Hunter Henry, New England Patriots (at Detroit Lions)

Despite a down Week 9, Henry ranks seventh among tight ends in PPR points over the last five weeks. He should bounce back in a big way Sunday in Munich, Germany. The Lions are allowing the most PPR points per game to tight ends—and by a sizable margin.

Tucker Kraft, Green Bay Packers (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

Kraft was the odd man out in Green Bay's rout of the New England Patriots, catching one pass for eight yards. Things aren't likely to get significantly better in this week's NFC North showdown with the Vikings—Minnesota allows the fewest PPR points per game to tight ends.

AJ Barner, Seattle Seahawks (at Las Vegas Raiders)

Barner had two catches for all of seven yards last week against the Cardinals, but one went for a touchdown, and he added a rushing touchdown on a goal-line "tush push." He has now found the end zone in two of Drew Lock's three appearances this season. The Raiders are also a top-five fantasy matchup for opposing tight ends this year.

The Jacksonville Jaguars already possessed a formidable defense. They are fifth in the league against the run, lead the AFC in scoring defense and sit fifth in fantasy points at the position.

But the Jaguars weren't satisfied—not by a long shot.

General manager James Gladstone swung a pair of significant trades on defense, dealing the team's first two picks next year (and then some) for safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis.

The former should help solidify a secondary that has struggled at times this year, while the latter will make it that much harder to run against the Jaguars.

And that new-look defense will debut against a Tennessee Titans offense that has been among the league's worst this season.

Last week was something of a do-or-die game for the Houston Texans—one of the first defenses off the board in many fantasy drafts over the summer has been a major disappointment to this point in the season.

Facing the Chargers has helped quite a few defenses this year get right, and last week was no exception—the Texans sacked Justin Herbert eight times and had their third double-digit fantasy week of the season.

The Los Angeles Rams finally got to see what their defense would look like with both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett last week against the Washington Commanders and the results were encouraging—Garrett logged three sacks in his first game action since the season opener in Australia.

And then there were two. There are now just two kickers in the NFL who have attempted at least 15 field goals without a miss. One is on a bye this week: Chase McLaughlin of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The other is Tyler Bass of the Buffalo Bills, who is now 19-for-19 for the season.

Green Bay Packers (vs. Minnesota Vikings)

The Green Bay offense is getting all the run, but the Packers defense has quietly been piling up big plays and now sits fourth in fantasy points ahead of Sunday's home date with the Vikings.

Evan McPherson, Cincinnati Bengals (vs. Pittsburgh Steelers)

McPherson hasn't exactly been piling up points, in part because he spends more time kicking PATs than field goals. But there's a reason why the Steelers are allowing the third-most fantasy points per game to kickers this year.

Last week against the Raiders, the 49ers turned five turnovers and a pick-six into the biggest fantasy stat line of the week. But don't expect a repeat—Dallas has been a bad fantasy matchup for defenses for years.

Will Reichard, Minnesota Vikings (at Green Bay Packers)

Reichard has been a top-five fantasy kicker this year in terms of fantasy points per game, but there is a lot of uncertainty around him this week, whether it's a new starting quarterback in Kirk Cousins or a bad fantasy matchup with the Packers.

The Colts defense is a risky streaming option, but a favorable matchup against a struggling Dolphins offense with Kyle McCord starting at quarterback puts Indianapolis in consideration.

Andre Szmyt, Cleveland Browns (vs. Houston Texans)

This game has several subplots, including Deshaun Watson facing his former team and a developing quarterback controversy. For fantasy managers, it also offers a favorable matchup for kickers, making Szmyt a streaming option.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Week 10 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Decisions for Fantasy Football Fringe Starters
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills continue to establish themselves as one of the top teams in the NFL this season. Their 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night wasn't pretty, but it was convincing.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills continue to establish themselves as one of the top teams in the NFL this season. Their 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night wasn't pretty, but it was convincing.

Fantasy football managers will look to similarly establish themselves well ahead of this year's fantasy playoffs. Notching a convincing win in Week 10, however, may require the use of more than a few fringe starters.

Injuries continue to be a factor, and four teams will be on bye this week—the Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Here are some early start/sit recommendations for point-per-reception (PPR) play.

Start: Ollie Gordon II, RB, Miami Dolphins

Running back Ollie Gordon II has emerged as a quality starter for the Miami Dolphins ever since they lost De'Von Achane to a season-ending knee injury. He's also become a strong option in fantasy, at least in good matchups.

Gordon has delivered 14 or more fantasy points in four of his last six games. However, he fell short of eight points in his last two, against the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions.

The good news is that Gordon should be back to a high level of production this week. The Dolphins are set to face the fading Indianapolis Colts, and they're likely to test the Colts' 30th-ranked run defense early and often.

Indianapolis has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

Sit: Corey Kiner, RB, New England Patriots

Patriots running back Corey Kinder is set to get his own starting opportunity. TreVeyon Henderson is out after experiencing a medical emergency, and Rhamondre Stevenson is set to miss some time with a knee injury .

Kiner is the next man up, and he's already been an established part of New England's offense. The second-year back has appeared in all nine games and has logged 50 carries.

Managers should strongly consider scooping up Kiner off the waiver wire, and he's only rostered in six percent of fantasy leagues. However, they shouldn't be eager to thrust him into the starting lineup against Detroit.

Kiner hasn't been heavily involved in the passing game (2 catches), which limits his PPR floor. The Lions, meanwhile, have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs.

Start: Jakobi Meyers, WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Parker Washington is now the unquestioned No. 1 receiver for the Jacksonville Jaguars. However, Jakobi Meyers is still an important piece of the passing puzzle.

Meyers, who was acquired last year in an in-season trade, has been targeted 37 times this season and has caught 28 of those passes. He has been a matchup-based streamer in fantasy, and he has disappointed at times. However, he has reached double-digit fantasy points in two of his last three games.

Last week, Meyers caught four passes and delivered 10.5 fantasy points against the Baltimore Ravens. This week, he'll have a very favorable matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Tennessee has looked like a more competitive squad in recent weeks, but it has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing receivers than any other team.

B/R's Week 10 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings

Jahan Dotson has spent the season as the Atlanta Falcons' No. 2 receiver opposite Drake Maye. His fantasy production has been erratic, but he's had some solid outings in favorable matchups.

Dotson has delivered double-digit fantasy points three times and has topped seven points in four of his past six games. However, he has disappeared in the offense at times, as the Falcons have focused on getting the ball to London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts.

This past week, Dotson caught just two passes on two targets.

London is probably worth trusting against a stiff Kansas City Chiefs defense this week, but Dotson is not. The Chiefs have surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers this season.

Managers with other options at receiver should explore them.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Week 10 Waiver Wire Top Pickups and Drops After Evaluating Week 9 Box Scores
articles.summary: Week 10 will begin with Thursday night's battle between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders. Both NFC East contenders have experienced season-ending injuries to key players, and many fantasy managers can likely relate.
articles.body:
Week 10 will begin with Thursday night's battle between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders. Both NFC East contenders have experienced season-ending injuries to key players, and many fantasy managers can likely relate.

Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin are only two of the marquee fantasy players who have been lost for the year. Arizona Cardinals wideout Michael Wilson is the latest.

Fortunately, managers may be able to find capable fill-ins on the waiver wire this week.

Here, we'll dive into what we saw in Week 9 and identify some top pickups and drops for Week 10. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) play.

New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith had a rough outing in Week 9, finishing with only 7.9 fantasy points. However, it's worth noting that he faced a stiff Kansas City Chiefs defense and was without wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion).

Smith has actually been a solid streamer for most of the season and yielded at least 19 fantasy points in each of his previous two games. He should have a good chance to bounce back this week against the Buffalo Bills.

Buffalo's defense looked terrific on Monday night, but it was playing a Minnesota Vikings offense that has struggled all year. For the season, the Bills have surrendered an average of 16.8 fantasy points to opposing QBs.

The Jets will likely have to throw often to keep pace with Josh Allen and Co., and they could have Wilson back in the lineup. Smith is only rostered in 22 percent of fantasy leagues.

Add: Corey Kiner, RB, New England Patriots

To be clear, New England Patriots running back Corey Kiner isn't an ideal option for Week 10. He hasn't been regularly used in the passing game, and he'll face a Detroit Lions defense that has been very, very good against the run.

However, Kiner is a veritable must-add because of New England's backfield situation. TreVeyon Henderson is out indefinitely after experiencing an unexpected medical issue. Rhamondre Stevenson is set to miss multiple weeks with a knee issue.

Kiner has logged 50 carries in a limited role this season, and he ran for 55 yards and a touchdown on Sunday. He should see a high volume of carries in Weeks 10 and 12—the Patriots are on bye in Week 11—and should carry a higher floor than most other waiver targets.

Kiner is rostered in only six percent of fantasy leagues.

If you haven't watched the Houston Texans over the last couple of weeks you may have missed the fact that Tank Dell is back. Houston's shifty sparkplug of a receiver caught four passes for 105 yards and a touchdown in Week 9.

Dell provided managers with 20.5 fantasy points.

This week, the Texans will visit the Cleveland Browns, who have a good overall defense but who have experienced breakdowns in the secondary. The Browns have surrendered an average of 24.1 fantasy points to opposing receiver groups this season.

Dell is a reasonable option for Week 10 and a must-add for the rest of the season. He is rostered in 23 percent of fantasy leagues.

Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold didn't play in Week 10 because of quad and rib injuries. He's already been ruled out for Week 10, and it's unclear when Darnold will return.

Given Darnold's erratic play and turnover issues this season, it's safe to drop him in most formats.

Minnesota Vikings running back Jordan Mason is in a committee backfield and in a bad offense. He also isn't regularly used in the passing game, as teammate Aaron Jones often is.

Mason reached double digits back in Week 1, but hasn't reached seven fantasy points in any other game this season. He's a moderate bench option in deeper leagues but can be dropped for waiver targets in most formats.

Marvin Harrison Jr. got a fresh start when he was traded to Houston and reunited with quarterback C.J. Stroud. However, a new home hasn't resulted in improved production.

Harrison hasn't reached double-digit fantasy points in any game this season. With Dell back in the Texans' lineup, Harrison can be dropped in virtually all formats.

articles.title: Updated NFL Salary Cap Outlook for All 32 Teams After 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline came and went at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, and the football landscape looks a lot different than it did over the weekend.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline came and went at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, and the football landscape looks a lot different than it did over the weekend.

We saw a couple of teams sell significant pieces ahead of the deadline. The Tennessee Titans, for example, dealt standout defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons a couple of weeks ago and traded star safety Amani Hooker on Tuesday. The Indianapolis Colts chose to hang onto quarterback Daniel Jones and running back Jonathan Taylor. However, they traded several other notable players.

On the other end of the spectrum, we saw the Jacksonville Jaguars spend big at the deadline, bringing in Jordan Davis, Davon Godchaux, and Jessie Bates III.

Here, we'll recap some of the biggest deadline deals and take an updated look at every team's salary-cap situation post-deadline.

Grades for all of this week's trades can be found here.

Trade Deadline Recap and Cap Implications

Unsurprisingly, the Titans and Colts are now near the top of the league in terms of effective 2026 cap space. Indianapolis kept its biggest players but traded Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen, and Josh Downs over the past couple of weeks.

The Atlanta Falcons are also near the top after trading Bates. The Jaguars are near the bottom of the league in 2026 cap space, and one of their deals will impact them in the future, too.

While Bates and Godchaux are both set to be free agents in 2027, Davis is signed through 2029. Due to the structuring of his contract, though, he'll only carry a cap hit of $4.8 million next season.

The Los Angeles Chargers agreed to trade standout linebacker Daiyan Henley to the rival Denver Broncos. The Cincinnati Bengals tried to acquire edge-defender Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles. However, Cincinnati ultimately pulled the plug on the deal after realizing that the move would likely cost a third-round pick due to the nature of the compensatory pick formula.

The biggest deal of Tuesday, of course, involved the Minnesota Vikings' acquisition of quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Las Vegas Raiders traded their starter to Minnesota and will now turn to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.

Minnesota, meanwhile, will reunite Cousins with head coach Kevin O'Connell for the remainder of the season. The Vikings will have financial options with Cousins next offseason.

It's also worth noting that, now that the deadline has passed, all players who are released are subject to waivers. Before the deadline, vested veterans were not subject to waivers and would instead become immediately free to sign with another team upon being released.

The free agent pool may not be particularly deep right now, but we have an idea of which teams can afford to spend over the second half of the season.

Looking ahead at 2027, the Falcons, Arizona Cardinals, Los Angeles Chargers, Miami Dolphins, and Detroit Lions lead the league in projected cap space . The Baltimore Ravens, Buffalo Bills, Houston Texans, Chicago Bears, and Jaguars make up the bottom five.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Colts' Decision to Keep Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Multiple factors reportedly contributed to the Indianapolis Colts' decision to hang onto running back Jonathan Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones through the trade deadline.
articles.body:
Multiple factors reportedly contributed to the Indianapolis Colts' decision to hang onto running back Jonathan Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones through the trade deadline.

According to ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler , the Colts wanted a first-round pick or something equivalent in a trade for Taylor, and that offer never came through.

Regarding Jones, Fowler noted that the Colts are "much more comfortable" with him under center than Anthony Richardson Sr., and Graziano added that since none of his $38 million salary for 2027 becomes guaranteed until March, the Colts can still move on from him fairly easily after the season if they so choose.

Indy began its fire sale a couple of weeks ago, trading guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers.

That led to rumors and speculation regarding Taylor and Jones being next, but the only trade the Colts ended up making Tuesday on deadline day was sending wide receiver Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs.

However, that doesn't mean there wasn't interest from teams in acquiring Taylor and Jones.

According to Fowler, the Denver Broncos "gave it a run" to acquire Taylor, but they weren't "comfortable" with what Indianapolis wanted in return.

The 27-year-old Taylor is the Colts' best player and their unquestioned face of the franchise.

A three-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro, Taylor has rushed for at least 1,400 yards each of the past two seasons, and through nine games this season, he has rushed for 656 yards and eight touchdowns.

Graziano wrote that the "buzz" surrounding Taylor as a trade candidate "never lined up with the Colts' desire to trade him."

Taylor is under contract for two more years, so there was no obvious need for the Colts to move him, especially if they have designs on bouncing back and contending for a playoff spot next season.

Trading Jones perhaps would have made more sense given his struggles and the idea that the Colts may try to pursue a different quarterback during the offseason.

It is unlikely that interest in Jones came anywhere close to the interest Taylor generated, but Fowler reported that Jones was "likely" the Minnesota Vikings' backup option if they did not land Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders.

The Vikings were in desperate search of a quarterback with Kyler Murray injured and Carson Wentz struggling, and they got their man in Cousins.

Like most Colts players, Jones has struggled through a difficult 2026, completing 60.3 percent of his passes for 1,722 yards, six touchdowns and 10 interceptions, while posting a 2-7 record.

Prior to tearing his Achilles last season, Jones was enjoying a career year, completing 68.0 percent of his passing attempts for 3,101 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight picks through 13 games.

Trading Jones at the deadline would have meant doing so when his value was at his lowest, so there may have been more value in keeping him and hoping he improves as he continues to get further removed from a devastating injury.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson Trade Pursued by Giants, New NFL Rumors Detail Talks After Jonathan Taylor Links
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor wasn't the only marquee running back the New York Giants made a push for prior to the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Jonathan Taylor wasn't the only marquee running back the New York Giants made a push for prior to the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday.

Per ESPN's Jordan Raanan, the Giants at one point made a call to the Atlanta Falcons to ask about Bijan Robinson's availability.

There was no indication from Raanan about how long the call lasted, nor if the Falcons even entertained the idea of moving Robinson.

Atlanta, despite being in the race in a muddled NFC South, did opt to sell before the trade deadline by trading Jessie Bates III and Ryan Neuzil.

Robinson is obviously in a different class of player than either of them. Bates and Neuzil are both 29 and in the final year of their current contracts, so it's safe to assume they would have left as free agents in the offseason.

The Falcons gave Robinson a three-year, $75 million contract extension in August that ties him to the organization through the 2030 season.

Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported on Sunday that New York offered a second- and fifth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for Taylor.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh didn't specifically confirm the offer or interest in Taylor, but suggested after Sunday's win over the Philadelphia Eagles they were having discussions about potential moves they could make.

"I'm not saying that report's not true. Those conversations are taking place," Harbaugh said . "If something happens for any player, can't talk about any [specific] player because they're with other teams right now, but we're not ruling anything out."

Nothing wound up coming out of the rumors because the Colts held onto Taylor through the deadline. Robinson would have been an even bigger swing since he is arguably the best running back in the NFL right now and a more versatile player because of his ability as a receiver.

New York put itself in position to potentially take a big swing by playing much better than anyone anticipated this season. Harbaugh has the Giants in first place in the NFC East going into Week 10.

Despite looking at Taylor and Robinson, the Giants wound up not making any moves before the deadline passed and will move forward this season with the group that has carried them to a 5-2-1 record.
