articles.title: Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders QB Decision Revealed Ahead of Browns' Game vs. Texans
articles.summary: Despite Shedeur Sanders' strong showing in an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints this past weekend, Deshaun Watson will return to a starting role against the Houston Texans on Sunday.
articles.body:
Despite Shedeur Sanders' strong showing in an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints this past weekend, Deshaun Watson will return to a starting role against the Houston Texans on Sunday.

Watson missed the Browns' 23-22 defeat in Week 9 due to a concussion, but he will be back in the lineup against his former team in Week 10. Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot first reported the news.

Each of the Browns' first eight games this season were started by Watson, who led Cleveland to a 5-3 record.

Watson and Sanders competed for the starting job during training camp and the preseason, and Browns head coach Todd Monken somewhat controversially decided to go with Watson.

The results of that choice have proved to be solid, though, as Watson is completing 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and just three interceptions, while also rushing for 217 yards and a score.

However, Sanders showed against New Orleans just how dynamic he can be, throwing for 297 yards, two touchdowns and no picks.

That included a 39-yard touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr. in overtime, which would have been the game-winner had Cleveland converted the ensuing two-point conversion.

The 24-year-old Sanders went 3-4 as a starter during his rookie season in 2025, although he only managed seven touchdowns compared to 10 interceptions.

He looked far more efficient in his first start of 2026, but it apparently wasn't enough to supplant Watson as the starter.

Watson played his first four NFL seasons with the Texans, and Sunday will mark only his second start against Houston since getting traded to the Browns prior to the 2022 campaign.

It will be a massive game for both teams as it relates to their playoff hopes, as the Browns are 5-4, while the Texans are 3-5.

articles.title: NFL Legend Drew Brees Talks Saints, Hall of Fame, Josh Allen, Caleb Williams & More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints legend Drew Brees knows the NFC South is probably a step below the rest of the divisions this season.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints legend Drew Brees knows the NFC South is probably a step below the rest of the divisions this season.

But he also knows that means opportunity for his former team.

"The division is wide open," Brees told Bleacher Report when discussing the Saints. "They're right there, it's all in front of them. You take care of your division games and win the ones you're supposed to, then you have a great shot at being a division winner and hosting a playoff game."

Winning the division and hosting playoff games was business as usual in New Orleans during Brees' tenure, but the team hasn't been to the postseason since he retired after the 2020 campaign. In fact, it finished in last place in the NFC South in each of the previous two seasons.

Yet there was reason for optimism coming into 2026 since Tyler Shough provided a boost as a rookie last season by going 5-4 as a starter. A second-year leap figured to be in play with more experience under his belt, and it was also the second year for head coach Kellen Moore.

Instead, inconsistency has been the defining theme on the way to a 3-5 start, although the silver lining is nobody has taken control of the division since all four teams each have three wins.

"Early on, it was just up and down," Brees said. "They lost that opening close game at Detroit and then had a big win on the road against Baltimore with a healthy Lamar Jackson. Cleveland's playing well right now, they just beat them in overtime. Also went on the road and beat the Giants when they were rolling. They've had some good wins, and yet you would just say maybe the lack of consistency has been it. That's what this game is about, you want to feel like you're doing all the little things and putting yourself in position to win."

Shough has been part of that inconsistency with some turnover issues undercutting his otherwise solid numbers while completing 66.2 percent of his passes for 1,986 yards, 14 touchdowns and six interceptions through eight games.

But Brees feels things are going to continue to improve as the season progresses.

"I would still call the Saints a young team from the perspective of a new coach from last year in Kellen Moore and a new quarterback from last year in Tyler Shough who only had a few starts going into the year," he said.

"They also drafted Jordyn Tyson, who is going to be an explosive player but gets hurt for the first half of the season. They were banged up on the defensive side for a while. Just getting guys healthy and finding your bread and butter, the things you want to hang your hat on for both sides of the ball. And when they do that, they'll slowly build a foundation and stack on top of that as they trend upward."

Ideally for the Saints, they can start building a foundation that comes anywhere close to the one in place when Brees was establishing himself as one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history.

The franchise icon was one of the defining players of his generation with a resume that includes a Lombardi Trophy, Super Bowl MVP, two Offensive Player of the Year awards, 12 seasons with more than 4,000 passing yards, four seasons with more than 5,000 passing yards, seven seasons when he led the league in passing yards and four seasons when he led in passing touchdowns.

The 13-time Pro Bowler finished his career with 80,358 passing yards and 571 passing touchdowns, and both marks are second in league history behind only Tom Brady.

Brees was a Hall of Fame lock and was officially inducted as part of the 2026 class alongside Larry Fitzgerald, Roger Craig, Luke Kuechly and Adam Vinatieri.

"I don't know if it ever completely sinks in," he said of being referred to as a Hall of Famer. "I've asked a couple other Hall of Famers who have been in for a long time, and that's exactly what they said. 'I still pinch myself.'"

He also greatly appreciated his entire football career building toward such a memorable induction ceremony.

"There were so many unbelievable moments at the Hall of Fame induction, especially just being able to have every single person who has been a part of the journey going back to when I was a kid to high school to college and the pros," Brees said. "Teammates, coaches, family members and others who were such an impactful part of the journey being there was amazing. It was amazing to be able to share it with them."

Brees has gotten to spend even more time with some of those important people in his life during retirement by coaching his sons at Santa Fe Christian in California as a passing game coordinator.

That experience is perhaps all the more notable since one of his quarterback contemporaries in Philip Rivers appears set to take the North Carolina State head coaching position. On Saturday, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported "all signs are pointing in that direction."

While Brees is happy for Rivers, his own alma mater in Purdue might not want to get any ideas.

"There are some guys where it's just in their DNA," he said. "He is certainly one of those guys. … This was inevitable, it's hard-wired into his system. I love coaching, I coach high school football right now. It's one of the most enjoyable things ever, this window of time and phase of life where I get the chance to be on the field for a couple hours a day with them and their friends and putting together gameplans and watching them struggle and then persevere. All the things we love about football. And I get a chance to do it firsthand with my kids.

"It's always in my system. But I just don't know if I'd be a head college coach, especially in today's era. But the desire to compete is always there."

That desire to compete has propelled him to incredible heights on the football field, which has given him an even bigger platform off the field for partnerships such as the one he has with ARS Pharma to further raise awareness for the need to be prepared in the face of severe allergies.

ARS Pharma makes neffy, which is a needle-free epinephrine nasal spray that can be used in an emergency situation when it comes to severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis.

"Millions of people around the world suffer from severe allergies, so you never know when a severe allergic reaction or potentially life-threatening situation could surface," Brees said. "So we have to be prepared. Especially with the holidays approaching with those big family get-togethers around the dinner table, it's important to understand what to do for somebody you know and love. This carries beyond the holidays. This is teachers and coaches and parents who are in environments with kids always being ready and prepared and understanding what to do."

When he isn't raising awareness and coaching his sons, Brees is still closely following the NFL and particularly enjoys watching another quarterback who will surely join him in Canton, Ohio, one day as a Hall of Famer.

"Josh Allen is a guy I love watching," he said. "Joe Brady, his coach, was an assistant with us with the Saints, so there's a lot of pieces of that system that are familiar. I love watching great coaches with great systems and gameplans you can watch unfold as the quarterback executes it."

About the only thing missing from Allen's list of accomplishments that includes a league MVP and four seasons with more than 4,000 passing yards is a Super Bowl ring, but Buffalo is well positioned to once again challenge for one following a 7-1 start.

And perhaps it will face another team that Brees has his eye on this season.

"I'm really interested to see how the Bears continue to trend," he said. "That Jeffery Simmons trade for them was huge. He's an impact player for them defensively, and not just in his production but now Devin Bush is having monster games at the linebacker position. Having that big guy in front of him gives him a lot more opportunities to make plays.

"And Caleb Williams can do a lot of incredible things. He's kind of one-of-one with some of the things he can do. And that offense with Ben Johnson is next level. That's one of the offenses I absolutely love watching."

Last season was Johnson's first as the head coach in Chicago, and he led the team to an NFC North title and Divisional Round appearance. This season brought a chance to build on that with continuity in place and Williams working in the system for a second straight year. That the Bears also bolstered their defense with the addition of Simmons only makes them more dangerous following a 7-2 start.

Brees knows what it takes to win a Super Bowl ring, and he likes what he sees so far in the Windy City.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins' Trade to Vikings From Raiders Detailed in New NFL Rumors After Deadline Day Deal
articles.summary: Before pulling the string on a trade for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings initially engaged in talks with the Las Vegas Raiders about the veteran quarterback last week.
articles.body:
Before pulling the string on a trade for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings initially engaged in talks with the Las Vegas Raiders about the veteran quarterback last week.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano , the Vikings "checked in" with the Raiders last week in an attempt to see what it might take to acquire Cousins if they decided to go that route.

However, according to Graziano, Minnesota "didn't get the sense" that Cousins was available prior to Sunday and the trade "only really came together" when it did due to the deadline otherwise the Vikings would have been out of luck.

"Had the deadline been two weeks from now, the Vikings might have decided to roll with their initial plan a while longer, especially if Murray is going to be healthy enough to play in the next week or so," Graziano wrote. "But if they didn't do a deal Tuesday, they weren't going to have a chance to fix their problem for the rest of the season.'

Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , the Vikings were "quietly" doing homework on potentially available quarterbacks in recent weeks but it wasn't until Murray's hamstring injury and Wentz's historically bad performance increased the urgency.

Pelissero added Cousins helped push the trade through by telling Raiders general manager John Spytek on Tuesday afternoon he wanted to rejoin Minnesota after previously playing for the team from 2018 to '23:

"With the trade compensation already in place, Cousins talked to his family, his longtime agent Mike McCartney, and Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell, whose offense he operated at a higher and more consistent level than any Vikings QB has since he left after the 2023 season. By midday Tuesday, Cousins had made up his mind and informed Raiders GM John Spytek: He wanted to go back to Minnesota, rejoin a team that's ready to make a playoff push, and potentially rewrite his complicated legacy at age 38.

"'So much respect for John Spytek and the Raiders organization,' McCartney told Pelissero Tuesday night of how the team handled the situation. "There aren't many leaders in this league who would've done that. Very appreciative of Spy."

It could reasonably be argued even if Murray was healthy or Wentz was adequate against Buffalo that the Vikings still should have pursued Cousins.

Of the 31 quarterbacks who have attempted at least 140 passes this season, Murray ranks 27th in success rate and QBR. He is 26th out of 35 quarterbacks with at least 100 snaps in EPA per play.

Minnesota's defense has shouldered a heavy burden for the team this season, and it has led to incredible success with a 6-2 record. Monday night saw the toll that an ineffective offense takes because the defense was on the field for nearly 43 minutes against Buffalo.

Even if that game represents an extreme outlier, the Vikings can't afford to take the risk of it happening because their margin of error is so slim due to how strong the NFC North is.

The Vikings sent a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders for Cousins. He is returning to Minnesota in the midst of one of his best seasons. The 38-year-old threw for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and a 64.1 completion percentage in nine starts with Vegas.

By comparison, Minnesota has used three quarterbacks in games this season. The group has combined to throw for 1,286 yards, eight touchdowns and a 60.9 completion percentage.

Cousins' familiarity with head coach Kevin O'Connell's system from their two years together in 2022 and 2023 should make for a smooth transition with him taking over the offense.

Even after Monday's loss, the Vikings still lead the NFL in points allowed per game. They are adding Cousins at the perfect time because their schedule for the next two weeks is road games against the Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers.

articles.title: New Cowboys Rumors Reveal George Pickens' Trade Market Prior to 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, many had wondered whether the Dallas Cowboys would move star wide receiver George Pickens, who is on an expiring contract.
articles.body:
Before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, many had wondered whether the Dallas Cowboys would move star wide receiver George Pickens, who is on an expiring contract.

However, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that the Cowboys "did not receive any trade calls" for Pickens, who is "happy in Dallas and didn't want to be traded."

Pickens is playing out the 2026 campaign on a one-year deal after receiving the franchise tag over the offseason. He hasn't been able to match the production of his breakout 2025 season, but he's been a solid No. 2 receiver for Dallas with 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns in eight games.

At 4-5, the Cowboys are struggling to maintain their position in the playoff hunt, so it would've been understandable if they tried to recoup assets by trading a coveted player like Pickens. Still, Fowler went on to note that teams looking for receivers weren't interested in paying a premium price.

"Teams in the receiver market weren't shopping in the high-end aisle, either, so the idea of a Pickens trade was a nonstarter," Fowler explained. "Plus, Dallas had no plans to deal him."

Pickens is currently dealing with shoulder and hamstring injuries, and he's considered questionable for the Cowboys' matchup against the San Francisco 49ers (7-1) on Sunday.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Rams' Ladd McConkey Pursuit Amid Puka Nacua, Davante Adams Injuries
articles.summary: Justin Herbert reportedly wasn't the only player about whom the winless Los Angeles Chargers rebuffed trade inquiries ahead of Tuesday's deadline.
articles.body:
Justin Herbert reportedly wasn't the only player about whom the winless Los Angeles Chargers rebuffed trade inquiries ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

The Los Angeles Rams are believed to have asked after wide receiver Ladd McConkey following the injuries that have sidelined Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.

"The Chargers said no to at least one Ladd McConkey inquiry," Fowler reported. "Teams I spoke to believe the Rams were the ones to make that call."

Rams to Consider Trade After Puka Injury

Fowler added the Rams ultimately "didn't seriously consider a receiver move" because the team expects Matthew Stafford to succeed in the short term before Nacua and Adams return later this season.

The news comes after NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Minnesota Vikings expressed interest in trading for Herbert before the Chargers "immediately shut down all inquiries."

McConkey, who is under contract through 2027, has gone from serving as Herbert's top target last season to recording just 17 catches with 286 yards and a touchdown in six games with the struggling Chargers' offense.

He missed his second game of the season last Sunday after suffering back spasms ahead of kickoff against the Houston Texans.

The Rams still might have hoped a fresh start for McConkey would help the wide receiver would help add some depth around Stafford in a campaign during which he has yet to play up to his 2025 MVP form.

Adams has not played since rupturing his hamstring Oct. 18. Fowler reported at the time Adams hoped to return "as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible."

Nacua could be hoping for a similar timeline given that the wide receiver has not yet been placed on injured reserve, although Rams coach Sean McVay has said the team expects to lose him for at least a month with an MCL and PCL sprain as well as turf toe in his right leg.

The Rams have also yet a few weeks to determine the future of Terrance Ferguson, who suffered a hamstring strain during his 21-day return-to-practice window on his way to coming back from an ankle injury. He must return by the end of that three-week stretch or sit out the rest of the season.

When asked about the possibility of trading for a wide receiver ahead of the deadline, McVay told reporters Monday he felt his team had to "look at all avenues."

The Rams have a Sunday road game against the Arizona Cardinals coming up before sitting out a Week 11 bye. McVay will hope a wide receiver room currently led by Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield can keep this team afloat until Adams and Nacua are able to return in what his team hopes will be the near future.

articles.title: Brian Thomas Jr.'s Jaguars Role Explained in New NFL Rumors After WR Wasn't Moved at Trade Deadline
articles.summary: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano weighed in on Brian Thomas Jr.'s value to the Jacksonville Jaguars after the team declined to trade him ahead of Tuesday's deadline.
articles.body:
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano weighed in on Brian Thomas Jr.'s value to the Jacksonville Jaguars after the team declined to trade him ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

Thomas has seemingly fallen behind other options including Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers on the Jaguars depth chart while recording just 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns in eight games this season.

The Jaguars "could have gotten a quality pick" for Thomas, who "garnered significant interest" ahead of the deadline, according to Fowler.

"They value Thomas, though his numbers don't reflect that. He has speed that demands defensive attention... Thomas was, quite easily, the most gifted athlete on the field when I visited Jaguars training camp," Fowler reported.

Graziano added Thomas' importance to the Jaguars has been made clear by injuries to receiving corps around the NFL, including on the Kansas City Chiefs (Tyquan Thornton), Los Angeles Rams (Puka Nacua and Davante Adams), San Francisco 49ers (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Christian Kirk).

"If something should happen to Jakobi Meyers or Parker Washington, the Jaguars believe Thomas is a player who could help them if he suddenly got thrust into a higher-volume role," Graziano reported.

Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said when asked about Thomas after the deadline his team appreciates having a wide receiver room with "a range of skillsets."

"His role, and what I imagine his contribution is going to be down the stretch here, is going to be notable," Gladstone said Tuesday about Thomas.

The Jaguars loaded up by the deadline by adding safety Jessie Bates III alongside defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux in what has been a clear push to build on the team's 6-2 start to make a playoff run this winter.

Thomas has caught just one pass in the last month. Jaguars coach Liam Coen could look to find a way to involve him more in the future, in part so the wide receiver is ready should he be called on to take on a larger role down the stretch.

articles.title: NFL trade deadline, odds: 3 bets that I like right now, including Fernando Mendoza to win Rookie of the Year
articles.summary: Our NFL handicapper gives three bets he likes after the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline was on Tuesday, and it sure was busy. There have been 18 completed trades since the start of the regular season, which included 23 of the 32 teams and 34 total draft picks changing hands (tied for the fourth most in the last 35 years).

QB Kirk Cousins going from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings to instantly supplant Carson Wentz and/or Kyler Murray as the team's starter was one of the biggest moves. The Jacksonville Jaguars were the most active buyers, bringing in multiple defensive starters, while the Indianapolis Colts offloaded multiple pieces for future draft capital.

As a bettor, my focus is instantly looking at the Week 10 games and futures market for value that ripples as an effect of these transactions. Usually the Week 10 games will see very quick market moves, but the futures market is a derivative place to attack for excellent post-trade deadline value.

Here are three futures worth placing now as it relates to the NFL trade deadline passing yesterday.

Los Angeles Rams to miss the playoffs (-118)

The Rams were in an incredibly difficult position at the trade deadline and were unable to get anything done. On the final offensive snap of their Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders, star WR Puka Nacua injured his right knee. He is now expected to miss several weeks, even if he doesn't land on injured reserve. WR Davante Adams is already on injury reserve, and so is their best pass-catching tight end Terrence Ferguson.

The Rams went from not needing to make a move to desperately hoping to add a wide receiver. They were unable to get anything done, which puts this team in a precarious situation over its final eight games.

If the season ended today, the 5-4 Rams would not be in the playoffs. The 49ers own the NFC West division and the Rams' record is not good enough to be a wild-card team. Based on the health of the team, it's going to be hard to play catch up. The offensive firepower is significantly compared to preseason expectations, and in this case not getting a deal done becomes a worst-case scenario as the WR room now hinges on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels. On a day that saw Keenan Allen and Josh Downs get traded from Indianapolis, it's difficult for Rams fans to know neither ended up in Los Angeles.

I am taking a small victory lap because one of my preseason NFL futures was Rams to miss the playoffs at +400, and now it is still a good take at -118. If you already bet it, you can add onto it small and bet it again.

Philadelphia Eagles under 4.5 wins (+110)

The Eagles are on their bye this upcoming weekend, so the best way to react to Philadelphia trading defensive tackle Jordan Davis is by looking at the season wins market. In the 18 total trades made this NFL season, the Eagles trading Jordan Davis was one of two transactions to include a first-round pick. That shows you the level of star power that just left the Philadelphia franchise and headed to Jacksonville.

The soft tank is on in Philadelphia. This team has lost seven straight games and they are without QB Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season. After turning to Tanner McKee at QB after Hurts' injury news broke, they quickly stopped that experiment, signed Joe Milton off the Cowboys practice squad and he is now starting. I truly think the Eagles know this season is lost, they don't want to win and prefer to prioritize upcoming draft capital. In the NFL, the draft order is a direct reflection of the standings and the worse you do that season, the better your picks are.

The Eagles have a very forward-thinking front office. One reason they were able to get a first-round pick for Davis was because of his team-friendly contract. Davis was given a huge signing bonus when Philadelphia inked his deal, and thus his annual salary was lower and his trade value was higher. Those little edges the Eagles gain are indirect ways to show they will prioritize next season over squeezing out an extra win or two.

I expect Milton to remain the starter and players that are injured — like DeVonta Smith with a hamstring issue — to be kept out as long as possible. An injury that a player might have played through on a contending team will now be a reason to sit out.

I am betting the Eagles regular-season win total under 4.5, hoping they don't win three of their final eight games.

Fernando Mendoza to win Offensive Rookie of the Year (+300)

Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, has been announced as the Raiders starting QB with Cousins' departure. Mendoza is primed to make a run for Offensive Rookie of the Year over the second half of the season. His head coach is Klint Kubiak, who was the offensive coordinator of the Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks last season. Mendoza has the best pass-catching tight end in Brock Bowers to target. And of course, we can expect Raiders owner Tom Brady to be speaking with Mendoza regularly the rest of the season as well.

The other side of this is looking at Mendoza's competition for this award.

There have been no standout players who are leading the pack for OROY. The weak player pool here is why Mendoza now has the shortest odds simply by being named the starter. Broncos rookie RB Jonah Coleman and Titans WR Carnell Tate round out the top three with the shortest odds. Coleman had a stint on IR and is just now taking over the Broncos backfield. Tate just missed the last Titans game with his own injury and is in a crowded room of skill players in Tennessee.

Fourth and fifth in the odds are Cleveland Browns wideouts Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, each of whom takes away from the other's upside to win this award.

It seems like chalk, but going for the ceiling outcome on Mendoza's rest of season is worth playing into at 3-to-1 odds.

articles.title: Giannis Questioned About 'Losing Sleep' amid Heat Struggles and Doc Rivers' Controversial Comments
articles.summary: Doc Rivers' recent comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo have not had any impact on the two-time NBA MVP.
articles.body:
Doc Rivers' recent comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo have not had any impact on the two-time NBA MVP.

Asked by The Athletic's Sam Amick if he was "losing sleep" over what Rivers said about his experience with Antetokounmpo, the Miami Heat star responded in very definitive fashion.

"Hell no," Antetokounmpo said. "Losing sleep? Hell no."

Giannis 'Speechless' After Doc's Comments 🎥

During an appearance on The Bill Simmons Podcast last week, Rivers explained Antetokounmpo was not always easy to coach because of how he liked to play:

"I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude," Rivers said. "He's interesting. He's not easy. He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy. ... He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it.

"I wish he learned how to execute better. He's one of those guys ... that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team. And I told Giannis this, the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shoot-arounds to lock in on execution. And now he has a coach [Erik Spoelstra] who is as good as there is in execution."

Rivers later i ssued an apology with Marc J. Spears of Andscape relaying what the former Milwaukee Bucks head coach told him he was trying to convey in his original comments.

If there has been a criticism of Antetokounmpo's game, it's the lack of development in his shooting ability. He has addressed it in the past even though it's still not what he is primarily known for.

Rivers coached Antetokounmpo for three seasons after being hired by the Bucks midway through the 2023-24 campaign.

Milwaukee made the playoffs in each of Rivers' first two years, losing in the first round both times. His final year in 2025-26 saw the Bucks finish 32-50, their worst record since Giannis' rookie season in 2013-14 (15-67).

Antetokounmpo finished top four in MVP voting in each of Rivers' first two years with the Bucks. He averaged 30.4 points, 11.7 rebounds and 6.5 assists per game in 140 starts during that period.

Milwaukee's struggles last season led to Rivers resigning from his position. Antetokounmpo was traded to Miami in July after spending 13 years with the Bucks.

articles.title: Drew Brees Talks 'Monday Night Football' Aspirations amid Troy Aikman Contract Rumors
articles.summary: Drew Brees is throwing his hat into the ring as a potential successor to Troy Aikman should the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback leave ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast.
articles.body:
Drew Brees is throwing his hat into the ring as a potential successor to Troy Aikman should the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback leave ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast.

Brees told Front Office Sports' Baker Machado (h/t Michael McCarthy ) he would "of course" be interested in the MNF job if it became available.

"At the end of the day, I aspire to be the best at what I'm pursuing," Brees, who is currently a Fox Sports analyst, told Machado (h/t McCarthy). "I love broadcasting and I love my team. And I love being able to broadcast games every week."

Aikman has said he will be a "free agent" when his ESPN contract expires after this year.

Brees started his media career at NBC Sports as an NFL and Notre Dame analyst but split from the network after just one year in 2022.

The former quarterback was featured on ESPN's Monday Night Countdown in 2024, then arrived at Fox Sports as an NFL analyst in November 2025 to work alongside Adam Amin and Kristina Pink.

Brees isn't currently working in a primetime slot. His team is next scheduled to call Sunday's 1 p.m. ET matchup between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers.

Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel reported back on Oct. 14 there was "tension" between Aikman and booth partner Joe Buck.

Aikman had not yet received a contract offer from ESPN, per Glasspiegel, while The Athletic's Andrew Marchand reported in September Buck had already agreed to a $108 million extension.

When asked about that report in an Oct. 15 appearance on Dallas-Fort Worth's 96.7 The Ticket , Aikman said his plan was to "broadcast through this season."

"I'll be a free agent at the end of the year, and kind of see what happens," Aikman said. "But I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this year does hold, and with the Super Bowl and all that, and where my next landing spot might be."

Even if Aikman and ESPN split at the end of the season, Brees would have plenty of competition for the Monday night gig. Former Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo and Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay have been speculated as potential candidates, while The Athletic's Andrew Marchand reported Fox Sports analyst Greg Olsen is "widely considered" the favorite to take over for Aikman.

articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: While other NFC contenders loaded up at deadline, Rams and Lions were quiet
articles.summary: The trade deadline was active, but not in Los Angeles or Detroit.
articles.body:
The theme of the trade deadline seemed to be contenders being more aggressive than ever before in their pursuit of a Super Bowl, particularly in the NFC.

That's what made the inactivity of the Detroit Lions and Los Angeles Rams a bit startling.

The Seattle Seahawks, Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers all made trades to help themselves now. The Green Bay Packers did not, but they're getting Micah Parsons back soon and they're relying on that being a big midseason addition. The 49ers did the least of that group, but they're also having the best season in the conference and starting to get a little healthier. And we don't need to count anyone in the NFC East or NFC South as a contender.

The only move the Rams or Lions made was Detroit trading a sixth-round pick to the Jets for safety Andre Cisco, who was a part-time starter for a bad New York team.

Let's start with the Rams, because they had the biggest need and their inactivity goes against their normal mode. The Rams have lost Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to injuries, and don't know if they'll be back before it's too late. They're dreadfully thin at receiver for the next few weeks, at least. The Rams have gone from preseason Super Bowl favorite to probably a slight underdog to even make the playoffs. Yet, they did not make a trade before the deadline. The Rams could argue, like the Packers, that adding Myles Garrett back is their in-season addition. But that doesn't help at receiver, and it's hard to believe the Rams have championship upside building a passing game around three or four tight ends and nothing else. It seems like the Rams put three-quarters of their chips in the middle, then folded.

The Lions probably could have used a cornerback or linebacker nearly as much as the Rams needed a receiver, but they did nothing other than a low-cost move to add Cisco. Detroit's defense probably isn't good enough to win a championship, and their fans will be frustrated after seeing other teams, particularly in the NFC North, make moves. They were clamoring for a cornerback for weeks and Jack Campbell's injury left them with a weakness at linebacker. Those areas of need still exist.

The Rams have a "forget them picks" attitude but it still has a limit. They gave up a lot to get Garrett and Trent McDuffie in the offseason. They might have also privately seen a team that is slipping further from being a Super Bowl contender and didn't want to chase their losses. The Lions didn't want to pay the escalating prices to make a huge move on the back end of their defense, and while that might be prudent for the long haul, Detroit fans don't want to be patient anymore. Maybe the Lions or Rams still make a deep playoff run, but they'll have to do it against teams that got much better over the past couple weeks.

Panic meter: The Rams and Lions are still good, but everyone around them got better.

Is now the right time for Fernando Mendoza?

The biggest secondary domino from the trade deadline moves happened with the Las Vegas Raiders. Trading Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings kicked off the Mendoza era. The No. 1 overall pick will be the team's starter going forward.

The timing isn't perfect. The next two games for the Raiders are against the Seahawks and Broncos, two of the toughest defenses in the NFL. The Broncos game is at Denver, which is a tough place to play.

It could be rough for Mendoza early on. The Raiders had to make the move when the Vikings offered a third-round pick for a 38-year-old quarterback who was probably starting only two more games for them anyway. Two games won't ruin the rookie but he's in for a welcome to the NFL moment or two.

Panic meter: Mendoza will be fine but expect some early struggles.

Rhamondre Stevenson has an injured tendon in his knee, TreVeyon Henderson has been out with a murky injury and that led people to believe the Patriots could trade for a running back. That didn't happen.

No running backs moved at the trade deadline. The Colts were reportedly asking way too much in return for Jonathan Taylor (more on Indianapolis in a moment) and perhaps the prices of others like Tony Pollard were egregious too. But now the Patriots move forward for a while with Corey Kiner as the lead back. That will put more pressure on Drake Maye, who is coming off a poor game against the Packers. The dream of contending in the AFC East is slipping away. Will the Patriots be a playoff team?

Panic meter: The Patriots should still sneak in the playoffs, but a running back trade would have been nice.

The Colts traded an eight-time Pro Bowl guard, a three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle. a six-time Pro Bowl receiver and a 25-year-old receiver who has shown promise, and somehow they didn't get a first- or second-round pick back for any of them.

The Colts got a lot of mid-round picks back for Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, but they didn't seem to maximize the value of any of them other than perhaps Allen. Buckner's return of a fourth-round pick seemed quite light given what some other defensive tackles went for. And the Jonathan Taylor situation was just odd.

The Colts reportedly received offers of a second-round pick and more for Taylor and passed. Taylor is a great player but he's a running back on a team with a long rebuild ahead of it. It made little sense to hold on to him. But the Colts, who don't have next year's first-round pick due to the Sauce Gardner trade, don't have much of a plan.

Panic meter: The Colts have a long rebuild ahead and this isn't a good sign it'll go well.

The Bengals can argue that trading the 10th overall pick of the draft for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II in the offseason was their big move. But some more might have been nice.

The Bengals are getting an MVP-level season from quarterback Joe Burrow, their offensive line is better than it has been in years and the defense has been competent. That defense could be better, though. Couldn't they have outbid the Broncos for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, who went for fourth- and fifth-round picks?

The Bengals' ownership has always been ripped for being cheap and maybe that was part of the team making no moves before the deadline. Either way, it's a team that should have Super Bowl hopes and might regret not doing anything to improve itself with another trade.

Panic meter: The Bengals are good but might ultimately find they're a piece or two away.

articles.title: Browns confirm no quarterback controversy as Deshaun Watson reclaims starting job over Shedeur Sanders
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson will reclaim his starting role for the Cleveland Browns despite Shedeur Sanders' near-overtime heroics against the New Orleans Saints.
articles.body: There appears to be no quarterback controversy for the Cleveland Browns. Shedeur Sanders was just one completion away from giving the Browns a wild overtime win over the New Orleans Saints this past weekend, as Deshaun Watson missed the Week 9 contest. However, Watson will recapture his spot as the team's starting quarterback on Sunday. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Watson entered concussion protocol last week and was actually cleared ahead of the game against the Saints, but the Browns rocked with Sanders anyway. The Colorado alum had impressive numbers, going 19-for-31 for 297 passing yards and two touchdowns - a 64-yard score to KC Concepcion in the fourth quarter and a 39-yard catch-and-run to Harold Fannin Jr. in overtime. Cleveland went for a two-point conversion and the win, but the New Orleans pass rush immediately pressured Sanders. He scrambled to his right before throwing an incomplete pass intended for Denzel Boston, ending the game. Watson is in the final year of his dreaded five-year, $230 million contract that the Browns have all but admitted to regretting. Sanders, once thought of as a top-five pick, fell to the fifth round of last year's NFL Draft and entered the season as the third-string quarterback behind Joe Flacco and fellow rookie Dillon Gabriel. TOM BRADY ADMITS TO MORE MOTIVATION AFTER DEFLATEGATE SUSPENSION, REVEALS WHAT HE DID WHILE AWAY FROM PATRIOTS Flacco was traded, and Gabriel suffered a concussion, bringing Sanders into the fold, but when he won his first NFL start, he was the starter for the remainder of the season. Watson, however, returned from a torn Achilles, and it never quite seemed like his job as a starter was in doubt, as long as he was healthy. In his eight games - his most since 2020 - Watson has completed 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Sanders is 3-5 as a starter - he threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 picks in his eight games last year (seven starts). OutKick's Dan Zaksheske contributed to this report.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Midseason Awards: Kenneth Walker III earns MVP — see who else won some hardware
articles.summary: It's time to hand out some fantasy football hardware as we push past the season's midpoint.
articles.body:
No matter the subject, awards are fun. Sports awards, movie awards, silly awards — I'm here for all of it. Get me to the red carpet, let the photos pop, let's have a night with the stars.

Today's assignment is to hand out some Fantasy Football hardware after nine weeks of the 2026 season. Get out your snappy tuxedo and let's laugh, cry and celebrate together.

The Seahawks always viewed Walker as a committee back, but credit the Chiefs for imagining something bigger. Walker leads the NFL in rushing yards per game, he's up to a juicy 5.5 YPC, he's on pace for his busiest receiving season ever and he's basically getting his mail in the end zone these days (11 total touchdowns). It's no surprise that 54.5% of the top 500 Public League teams in Yahoo have a Walker share.

Runners-up: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, Jahmyr Gibbs

One-Man Show Award: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seahawks

Everything else in the Seattle offense has gone sideways this year — Sam Darnold has taken a major step back (and gotten hurt), the other receivers aren't popping, not much is working in the backfield. It doesn't keep JSN down. He's just one touchdown away from the 10 he bagged last year, and could make a run as the NFL's first-ever 2,000-yard receiver. To keep producing against defenses that are designed to stop just one guy, it's utterly amazing.

Runner-Up: Tony Pollard, Bucky Irving, Trey McBride

Crash Team of the Year: Los Angeles Chargers

It all sounded so nice in the summer — new offensive coordinator, fixed offensive line, star QB finally in the right spot. But Mike McDaniel's schemes have not worked, the OL quickly fell apart and Justin Herbert's mojo left early to beat the traffic. The Chargers still don't have a win, and it's not easy to find possible ones on their remaining schedule.

Waiver Add of the Year: Braelon Allen, Jets

Allen was too good to be true in his four weeks as the primary back, averaging 5.6 YPC and racking up 126.8 yards from scrimmage per game. It doesn't seem fair that Allen now has to share with Breece Hall again; the Jets somehow didn't do anything at the trade deadline.

Value of the Year: The Green Bay passing game

Sometimes the dots all connect. Underrated quarterback and play-caller. Leaky run-blocking offensive line. Streamlined WR room with ascending talent. Jordan Love (QB3), Christian Watson (WR3) and Matthew Golden (WR5) are all looking like league-tilting picks, and it's so much fun watching Love drop those gorgeous long passes on opponents every week. The Packers will struggle to run the ball against most opponents, so keep that passing volume coming.

Runners-up: Chuba Hubbard, Bucky Irving, Parker Washington, Jaylen Warren, Isaiah Likely

The offense ranks sixth in DVOA, the defense ranks 29th (hard to believe three are worse). Most of the production has centered around winning picks Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and Javonte Williams, but George Pickens should come around before long. Dallas starts every week figuring it needs 30 points to win, and some weeks, that's not even enough.

Runners-up: Lions, Bengals — some things never change.

Anti-Carnival of the Year: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The physical Bucs might steal the forever-dysfunctional NFC South this year, and if they do, they'll do it playing 1977 football. Tampa Bay runs the ball well, it stops everyone from running on them, and it leads the NFL in takeaways (this excellent defense is comically underrated). What Tampa Bay doesn't do is pass the ball much. Baker Mayfield had just 64 yards in the Week 7 win over Carolina, then followed it up with an 0-for-3 bizarro game against Atlanta in the rain. What year is it again?

Unintentional Grounding of the Year: Los Angeles Rams

The flashy Rams were tabbed as Super Bowl favorites in the summer, but injuries to Davante Adams and now Puka Nacua have canceled the flight. It's possible Matthew Stafford might be playing hurt, too. If the Rams are going to rally and make the playoffs, it will come on the strength of running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, and a suddenly-healing defense. But this isn't the fantasy blast we were dreaming about.

Runners-up: Broncos, Zay Flowers (we weep for the Lamar Jackson injury)

Most Underrated Star: Brock Purdy, 49ers

The Niners have been absurdly unlucky with WR injuries, but nothing seems to bother Purdy. He leads the NFL in QBR and sack avoidance, he's thrown 17 touchdowns against just five picks and he's offering surprising rushing chops. He'll be a factor in the MVP race.

Comeback of the Year: Kirk Cousins, Vikings

Remember when Cousins looked all but finished in Atlanta? Ah, that was so 2025. Cousins ripped off two outstanding months with the Raiders (20 TD passes, 97.1 rating) and is now seen as the savior for a Minnesota team that's been all defense and no offense. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison probably picked up Cousins at the airport.

Runners-up: C.J. Stroud, Chuba Hubbard, Joe Burrow, Malik Nabers

Bust of the Year: Ashton Jeanty, Raiders

We steer injured players away from this award, so Saquon Barkley and A.J. Brown can breathe easier. Jeanty has been outplayed by rookie Mike Washington Jr., and new coach Klint Kubiak has turned this backfield into a true committee of late. The offensive efficiency might tank in the second half, depending on how ready for play rookie QB Fernando Mendoza is.

Runner-up: Justin Jefferson, Marvin Harrison Jr., Justin Herbert

The Bears can't help you with a Week 10 bye, but their remaining schedule has a bunch of dream matchups (Saints, Lions twice, Bills), weather permitting. Caleb Williams is healthy again, and after a slow start, Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland are starting to pop. Let it rip.

Runner-up: Jaguars (if the Jacksonville defense doesn't mute the party)

articles.title: Travis Kelce Reacts to Josh Downs Trade, '100% Made' Chiefs Better After NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Travis Kelce approved of the Kansas City Chiefs' trade deadline maneuvering.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce approved of the Kansas City Chiefs' trade deadline maneuvering.

The Chiefs' trade for former Indianapolis Colts wideout Josh Downs could help the team expose defenses that are focused on stopping star running back Kenneth Walker III, Kelce said around the 26:30 mark of Wednesday's episode of his New Heights podcast .

"Man to man coverage, that's going to come up more than you think down the line," Kelce said. "When things get tight in the NFL, man coverage is what defensive coordinators go to. And when you've got a guy that you can trust in those kind of situations— and on top of that, I feel like in the middle of the field, he feels the zone coverages and what defensive voids, he's very good in all of that.

"And just to get another fast guy, another focal point for the defense to have to worry about in terms of run game, and having to relate the right way, and things like that, it 100 percent made our offense better."

The Chiefs sent 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks to the Colts and acquired a 2027 seventh-rounder while trading for Downs ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

Kelce wasn't the only member of the Chiefs to express appreciation for the trade. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes seemingly celebrated on social media shortly after the deal was finalized.

Downs requested a trade from the Colts last month partly because he knew "he had the potential to play alongside Mahomes and the rest of the Chiefs' stars on offense," ESPN's Nate Taylor reported.

He should add some speed to a Chiefs receiving corps that has been functioning without Tyquan Thornton, who suffered a significant ankle injury in early October that is expected to sideline him indefinitely.

The Chiefs are next scheduled to play Sunday against an Atlanta Falcons defense that ranked 20th in the NFL in passing yards before trading safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Former NFL Coach Rex Ryan Turns Himself in After Alleged Nashville Hit-and-Run
articles.summary: NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Former NFL coach Rex Ryan turned himself in Wednesday for allegedly hitting pedestrians with his car in Nashville and leaving the scene, police said.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Former NFL coach Rex Ryan turned himself in Wednesday for allegedly hitting pedestrians with his car in Nashville and leaving the scene, police said.

Two pedestrians had the right of way crossing a main street in downtown Nashville's popular tourist area last week when Ryan allegedly turned at a red light, running over the victims' feet, Nashville police said Wednesday. They suffered minor injuries, police said.

Ryan, an ESPN analyst, was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information or render aid and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal, according to court records, which did not identify an attorney for Ryan. All are misdemeanors. A judicial commissioner set Ryan's bond at $6,000.

Brady: Maye Gave 'Deli Meat' to Packers 😬

He was granted pretrial release Wednesday morning. Ryan is scheduled to appear in court next month.

Ryan is a former head coach of the Buffalo Bills and New York Jets, leading the Jets to the AFC Championship Game in consecutive years after the 2009 and 2010 seasons. His father, the late Buddy Ryan, was an NFL coaching legend who famously coordinated the 1985 Chicago Bears defense that was one of the best in history.

Since leaving coaching, Ryan is best known for his work at ESPN as one of the analysts on the network's NFL pregame show.

"We are aware and are in touch with Rex," ESPN said in a statement Wednesday. Ryan appeared Monday on "Get Up," a morning ESPN show taped in New York.

A phone number believed to be Ryan's had an automatic outgoing message, and a message could not be left.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins' 1st Reaction to Vikings-Raiders Trade Revealed, Opens Up on 'Mixed' Emotions
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins says he has "mixed" feelings about being traded back to the Minnesota Vikings in the middle of his first season with the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins says he has "mixed" feelings about being traded back to the Minnesota Vikings in the middle of his first season with the Las Vegas Raiders.

"I've got a lot of emotions right now that are mixed," Cousins said in an interview with Great Clips the day after the trade. "Always difficult to say goodbye, especially to people that mean a great deal to me, and there are so many of them here in Vegas.

"There's also a lot of people waiting for me in Minnesota that mean a great deal to me, that it was difficult to say goodbye to three years ago."

Report: Raiders Gave Cousins Trade Choice

Cousins also expressed excitement about getting another chance to win with the Vikings after getting only as far as the divisional round in his first stint with the team.

"I understand the challenge on the football field, there's a lot of work to go get done, but it would be really special," Cousins said. "If you're going to go win somewhere and have success, I wanted it to be in Minnesota."

Cousins first played for the Vikings from 2018 to 2023, a span that included two years with current Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell. He earned three Pro Bowl nods and one playoff win over that span.

He signed with the Falcons in 2024, then spent two seasons with the franchise before he inked a new deal with the Raiders to play in front of top draft pick Fernando Mendoza this season.

Cousins had led the Raiders to a 4-5 start by completing 64.1 percent of his passes with 2,340 passing yards and 20 touchdowns to eight interceptions prior to his trade.

"To the fans in Vegas, I just feel so grateful for how they welcomed me with open arms for the several months I was here. That includes teammates, the organization," Cousins said. "I really couldn't speak more highly of my time here in Vegas.

"To the fans in Minnesota, I'm thrilled to have a chance to come back, and to hopefully write the ending to a story, for me, that started eight, nine years ago when I first arrived."

The Vikings' defense has allowed the second-fewest yards against in the NFL so far this season, but the offense struggled behind Kyler Murray before he suffered a hamstring strain and was replaced last Monday by Carson Wentz.

O'Connell will hope slotting Cousins back into his offense can help the Vikings (6-2) snap a two-game losing streak and continue competing for a playoff spot in a stacked NFC North in which all four teams had earned at least six wins through Week 9.

articles.title: Cam Ward's QB1 Status Updated by Titans GM Amid Struggles, Jeffery Simmons, Amani Hooker Trades
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi left no doubt the team believes Cam Ward is its quarterback now and going forward, per comments to reporters at his press conference on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi left no doubt the team believes Cam Ward is its quarterback now and going forward, per comments to reporters at his press conference on Wednesday.

This has been a difficult season for the 1-7 Titans, and Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, has endured his fair share of struggles, although he just threw for a career-high 304 yards in a 43-36 overtime loss to the 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in his last game.

The Titans have been moving like a team with an eye toward the future, though, as they dealt their best player, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, to the Chicago Bears for a pair of first-round draft picks. Tennessee also moved safety Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills for a 2027 second-rounder.

There appears to be no question that Ward is the Titans' quarterback moving forward, though.

For the season, the former Miami star has completed 62.5 percent of his passes for 1,483 yards (6.0 yards per attempt), six touchdowns and five interceptions. He's also rushed for 112 yards and a pair of scores.

Ward's 78.7 quarterback rating is 27th among 31 qualified signal-callers, and his 49.0 QBR sits 23rd overall, per Pro Football Reference .

Those are concerning numbers roughly halfway through the season, and the Titans have also scored the fifth-fewest points per game (18.0) in the NFL.

However, Ward offered hope against the Bengals. Despite playing without wide receiver Carnell Tate, who leads the team with 413 receiving yards but unfortunately sat due to a shoulder injury, Ward completed 26-of-40 passes en route to his 304 yards and two scores. He also rushed for 41 yards as well and kept the Titans in a tough shootout with quarterback Joe Burrow, whose 23 TD passes lead the NFL.

The Titans had a bye week after that contest but now return to action Sunday in a tough matchup at home against a 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars team that added safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux before the trade deadline.

articles.title: Eagles' DeVonta Smith outfits Roman Catholic football team with cleats

DeVonta Smith is helping outfit the next generation of Philadelphia football players.

Under Armour Football shared the gesture in an Instagram video highlighting Smith's involvement. The gift connects one of Philadelphia's most recognizable current players with a school that has produced professional standouts, including Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receiver Marvin Harrison and former NFL receiver Will Fuller.

For Roman Catholic's players, the contribution brings support from an established NFL receiver to their own football experience. For Smith, it provides another connection to the Philadelphia community beyond his work with the Eagles .

articles.title: Dan Campbell Sends Clear Message After Lions’ Quiet NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Dan Campbell has weighed in on the Detroit Lions' quiet NFL trade deadline. Despite making just one move, the head coach remains confident in his team's dept...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions didn't make the splash many fans were hoping for at Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, but head coach Dan Campbell doesn't appear to be losing any sleep over it. In fact, Campbell sounds pretty confident about the roster general manager Brad Holmes has assembled.

Speaking to reporters Wednesday, Campbell was asked about Detroit's lack of activity and how he feels about his team heading into the stretch run of the season. His response was simple, and it certainly didn't sound like a coach who believes his team is missing a major piece.

"Feel good. We love our guys, man. We love our guys. …I think we're in a good spot here, man," Campbell said, according to The Athletic's Colton Pouncy.

That's a pretty strong endorsement considering the Lions' decision to stand pat while other NFL contenders made significant additions.

Dan Campbell Believes Lions Can Improve From Within

According to Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News, Campbell pointed to Detroit's continued improvement and expressed confidence in the team's depth.

"We're pretty good with depth right now," Campbell said.

Brad Galli of WXYZ-TV added that Campbell believes the Lions identified opportunities to improve internally early in the season, particularly on defense. And judging by Detroit's recent performances, the head coach believes that improvement is happening.

"When you're doing that, it's like 'That's what we thought it would be,'" Campbell explained. "A lot of things were looked at, but we feel pretty good right now."

The Lions have won four consecutive games to improve to 6-2, and their defense has taken noticeable strides during that stretch. According to Detroit's official team website , the unit has not allowed more than 21 points in any of its last four games.

That improvement appears to be a major reason Campbell feels comfortable moving forward with the players already in the building.

Detroit Lions Are Betting on Their Current Roster

Detroit's only trade deadline acquisition was veteran safety Andre Cisco, who arrived Monday in a deal with the New York Jets. The Lions initially agreed to send a 2028 sixth-round pick to New York, though the trade compensation was later changed to a 2029 sixth-round selection.

Of course, not everyone is thrilled with Holmes' approach. Detroit's decision to avoid a bigger move has already drawn criticism from Mike Valenti , particularly with the Lions dealing with injuries at linebacker.

The frustration is understandable, especially with Detroit trying to win its first Super Bowl. But as The Detroit News reported following Tuesday's deadline , the Lions ultimately chose not to pursue another deal after acquiring Cisco.

Campbell clearly believes the answers to Detroit's remaining questions can come from within. Whether that confidence is justified will become clearer as the Lions face tougher competition down the stretch.

For now, though, Campbell isn't interested in worrying about the moves Detroit didn't make. He likes his guys, and he's ready to find out just how far they can take this team.

articles.title: Former NFL coach Rex Ryan arrested on 6 charges
articles.summary: Ryan surrenders to police after two pedestrians are struck.
articles.body:
Former NFL head coach and current ESPN broadcaster Rex Ryan has surrendered to police in Nashville, Tennessee, and is facing six charges following an incident that left two pedestrians with minor injuries.

According to reports, Ryan allegedly struck both pedestrians with his truck while they were crossing Broadway from 4th Avenue shortly before midnight on November 5.

Metro Nashville Police said the pedestrians had the right of way and were crossing with a walk signal when the incident occurred.

In a statement, police explained that the vehicle initially continued driving before stopping at a red light near Broadway and Representative John Lewis Way. The pedestrians then approached the truck and confronted the driver.

"The pedestrians said the vehicle kept going, but stopped for the red light at Broadway and Representative John Lewis Way where they waved down the driver," police said. "They said he stepped out of the truck to argue with them, got back in, and drove away."

Ryan subsequently surrendered to authorities and now faces six charges related to the incident.

Ryan facing six charges following Nashville incident

The former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach has been charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information or render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal.

His bond was reportedly set at $6,000, and he is scheduled to appear in a Nashville courtroom on December 18.

The incident has created an unexpected headline for Ryan, who has remained a recognizable personality in the NFL media landscape since transitioning into broadcasting.

After a brief stint with the Arizona Cardinals in 1999, Ryan began his coaching career in earnest with the Baltimore Ravens in 1999, serving as a defensive line coach and helping the organization win Super Bowl XXXV against the New York Giants.

He eventually became Baltimore's defensive coordinator before landing his first head coaching opportunity with the franchise in 2008. Ryan later became head coach of the New York Jets, leading the team to consecutive AFC Championship Game appearances.

After being dismissed by the Jets in December 2014, Ryan was hired by the Buffalo Bills. However, his tenure ended following a loss to the Miami Dolphins on Christmas Eve in 2016.

Ryan eventually joined ESPN as an NFL analyst, becoming a familiar face on the network's football coverage. His upcoming court appearance will now put his off-field situation in the spotlight.

The New York Jets are running out of reasons to feel good about the 2026 NFL season, but the picture could look considerably different come spring. Another disappointing result, a 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9, has left the organization with plenty of questions to answer moving forward, particularly at the quarterback position.

If there's a silver lining, it's that the Jets (2-7) are sitting pretty in Round 1 of the 2027 NFL Draft. That could give them a legitimate opportunity to find that answer.

According to Tankathon, New York currently holds two of the first six selections and three of the first 13 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. If the season were to end today, the Jets would own the Indianapolis Colts ' first-round pick at No. 4, their own selection at No. 6 and the Dallas Cowboys ' pick at No. 13.

That's an impressive collection of draft capital, especially for a team with a potentially significant need at the game's most important position. The quarterback class could make that position even more valuable. Several quarterbacks are expected to be available in the 2027 draft, giving the Jets a chance to evaluate their options rather than enter the offseason with only one potential path toward finding a long-term answer.

Whether they use one of their premium selections or package multiple picks to move around the board, general manager Darren Mougey has the resources to make an aggressive move. Oh, and by the way, he may already have some interest in Oklahoma State Cowboys signal-caller Drew Mestemaker.

The Jets' situation offers something the organization has lacked in recent years: options. They could use one of those early selections on a quarterback, address other significant roster needs with the remaining picks, or explore a trade that puts them in position to secure their preferred prospect.

New York still has plenty of football left to play, and the draft order will change as the standings develop. But the opportunity is already taking shape. If the Jets are serious about finding their next franchise quarterback, they may have the draft capital to make it happen.

articles.title: Skip Bayless says Carson Wentz ‘can’t play football’ after Vikings performance vs Bills
articles.summary: Carson Wentz’s performance on Monday Night Football drew heavy criticism from everyone in the NFL community, and Skip Bayless joined in by going off on the q...
articles.body:
Carson Wentz's performance on Monday Night Football drew heavy criticism from everyone in the NFL community, and Skip Bayless joined in by going off on the quarterback.

The 33-year-old threw for 81 yards and completed only 8 passes out of 25 attempts, which meant he had a completion rate of only 32%. Wentz ended up with a passer rating of 8.9, which is the lowest for any player with 25 or more passes in the NFL since 2019.

His inability to get the ball to the end zone led the Vikings to suffer a 6-23 defeat and pushed them out of the top place in the NFC North.

This was Wentz's chance to prove that he could take over Kyler Murray as the starter, but he put on a horrific performance, which led to the Vikings deciding to trade for Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline, which was just a day after the game.

Skip Bayless believes Carson Wentz is not accurate consistently

Wentz was a regular starter in the league for 7 seasons. He was a second pick in the 2016 draft by the Philadelphia Eagles; however, he was never able to fulfil the promise he showed at North Dakota State.

In the games he has started, Wentz has thrown for over 23,000 yards and completed 62.7% of his passes. But none of that impressed Bayless, who fired shots at Wentz, discussing his performance on Monday Night Football.

"I have been hard on him. I was hard on Carson Wentz coming out of college before he got drafted. I didn't like him at North Dakota State. I didn't like his poise or his feel. He's one of those guys who's the prototype 6'5, 240-pound, rocket-arm quarterback who can't play football, and he's not accurate consistently. All he can do is throw it through a brick wall. Well, that's not how you win NFL games at the highest level," said Bayless on Gridiron.

With Cousins now set to take over the reins as the starting quarterback, Wentz's future with the Vikings could be questionable. They already have Kyler Murray, who can play as the backup.

He is definitely a good piece to have on a team, as he has proven experience starting games, which not a lot of backups in the league have. However, after his performance against the Bills, fans would definitely not be happy if they see him take snaps under center.

articles.title: ESPN analyst Rex Ryan arrested after allegedly striking 2 pedestrians with his truck, running over their feet
articles.summary: Rex Ryan faces six misdemeanor charges for his alleged actions.
articles.body:
Former New York Jets coach and current ESPN analyst Rex Ryan surrendered for booking Wednesday after being accused of striking two pedestrians with his truck , the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department confirmed.

The incident reportedly took place Thursday night in Nashville around midnight. Ryan was accused of turning at an intersection while two pedestrians had a walk sign. As Ryan turned his truck, he allegedly ran over two of the victims' feet. His truck also reportedly made contact with one of the victims' legs, per the police statement.

Ryan reportedly continued driving, though later stopped at a red light. He was flagged down by the victims and allegedly argued with them before getting back in his car and leaving the scene. The victims took photos of Ryan's license plate.

Ryan faces six charges in the incident. He was charged with two counts of "leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal," per police.

Ryan rose to prominence in the NFL as a defensive coordinator, following in his father Buddy Ryan's footsteps. Rex was then thrust into the spotlight when he took over as the Jets' head coach. His immediate success with the team, in addition to his personality, made Ryan a popular figure among fans.

After six seasons with the team, Ryan was fired in 2014. He quickly caught on with the Buffalo Bills, where he lasted two seasons before being dismissed.

Following his dismissal by the Bills, Ryan joined ESPN. He's been an NFL analyst at the network since 2016.

ESPN has yet to comment on Ryan's arrest.

articles.title: Chiefs sticking with Harrison Butker at kicker in Week 10 despite recent struggles
articles.summary: Harrison Butker will kick for the Chiefs against the Falcons in Week 10.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs will stick with Harrison Butker in Week 10, giving the kicker another chance to turn things around after weeks of struggles, head coach Andy Reid announced Wednesday.

After Sunday's win over the Jets, in which Butker missed another field goal attempt (a 51-yarder), Andy Reid said that he would "look at everything" to assess whether it was time to move on. Evidently, Reid decided to stick with his long-time kicker.

Butker, who has spent his entire 10-year NFL career with the Chiefs, has seen his field goal accuracy crater this season. He's missed seven field goals in eight games so far this year, going 12-of-19 on attempts. That 63% completion rate is a noticeable dip from his previous decade of experience. Prior to 2026, Butker converted on 88.4 of his field-goal attempts.

All but one of Butker's misses have come from lengths of 50-plus yards, indicating that he is being asked to take longer and longer attempts. But he has not risen to the challenge, receiving boos from the home crowd in Arrowhead Stadium in recent weeks after continuing to miss the uprights.

With Butker still holding the starting job, the team will not yet be turning to Justin Tucker, who joined Kansas City's practice squad at the end of October. Tucker has not played an NFL game since being released by the Baltimore Ravens in May 2025, after he was accused of sexual misconduct by more than a dozen women .

Even before his release, and subsequent suspension by the league , the former eight-time All-Pro had struggled: Tucker went 22-for-30 on field goals in 2024, with three of the misses coming under 50 yards, and also missed two extra points.

articles.title: Dick Hoak, longtime Steelers running back and coach, dies at 86
articles.summary: Hoak spent 45 years with the Steelers organization as a player and a coach.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers running back and coach Dick Hoak has died, the team announced on Wednesday . He was 86 years old.

Hoak, who was born just outside Pittsburgh in Jeannette, Pennsylvania, was a seventh-round pick by the Steelers in the 1961 NFL Draft out of Penn State. He would play all 10 of his seasons in the league with the franchise. In 1968, he was named to the Pro Bowl after rushing for a career-high 858 yards.

Following the 1970 season, Hoak announced his retirement. At the time, he was second on the franchise's all-time rushing list with 3,965 yards. He also finished with 25 touchdowns.

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dick Hoak, a legendary member of the Pittsburgh Steelers family," said Steelers President Art Rooney II in a statement . "Dick was part of the foundation of this organization and played an instrumental role in shaping the Steelers as both a player and coach during his 45 years with the team. "Dick represented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick's contributions to this organization spanned generations. "He was respected and admired by everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him. His legacy includes coaching some of the all-time great Steelers, including Franco Harris, Rocky Bleier, Jerome Bettis, and Willie Parker. "Our thoughts and prayers are with the entire Hoak family during this difficult time. He will always be remembered as a valued member of the Steelers family."

"Dick represented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick's contributions to this organization spanned generations.

"He was respected and admired by everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him. His legacy includes coaching some of the all-time great Steelers, including Franco Harris, Rocky Bleier, Jerome Bettis, and Willie Parker.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with the entire Hoak family during this difficult time. He will always be remembered as a valued member of the Steelers family."

Chuck Noll hired Hoak as the team's running backs coach two years after his retirement. He would hold that position for 35 years, working with the likes of Harris, Bleier and Bettis, among others while being a part of five Super Bowl-winning teams.

Hoak retired after the 2006 NFL season and in 2017 was part of the inaugural class in the Steelers Hall of Honor .

In 2025, Hoak was honored by the Pro Football Hall of Fame with its Award of Excellence , which recognizes significant contributors to the game in "behind-the-scenes" roles.

"I was pretty lucky," Hoak said in a 2020 interview with the Steelers website . "I played in Jeannette. I went to Penn State. I got drafted here, played here. I had some opportunities to leave. … I never left. It was my hometown.

"If I needed anything, I knew everybody. And I didn't want to move my kids around. Once you start that, I didn't want to do that. I was fortunate enough to go back to my hometown, live there all my life. I didn't have to move my kids. They all turned out pretty good. That's all I needed."
